title.en: Volume 106 Treatises 81: Selection and Examinations 1: Schools 1

sentences.zh: 志八十一

translations.literal: Treatise 81.
translations.idiomatic: Treatise 81

sentences.zh: 選舉一

translations.literal: Selection and Examinations 1.
translations.idiomatic: Selection and Examinations, Part 1

sentences.zh: 古者取士之法，莫備於成周，而得人之盛，亦以成周為最。

translations.literal: Among ancient methods for selecting scholars, none was more complete than that of the Western Zhou, and the fullness of men obtained was also greatest in the Western Zhou.
translations.idiomatic: Of all ancient methods for recruiting talent, none was more fully developed than that of the Western Zhou—and nowhere was talent gathered in greater abundance.

sentences.zh: 自唐以後，廢選舉之制，改用科目，歷代相沿。

translations.literal: From the Tang onward, the selection system was abolished and the examination curriculum was adopted instead, and successive dynasties followed this practice.
translations.idiomatic: From the Tang dynasty onward, the older selection system was set aside in favor of subject-based examinations, a practice successive dynasties retained.

sentences.zh: 而明則專取四子書及易、書、詩、春秋、禮記五經命題試士，謂之制義。

translations.literal: The Ming, however, exclusively took the Four Books and the Five Classics—Changes, Documents, Odes, Spring and Autumn, and Record of Rites—as topics to test scholars, calling this regulated exposition.
translations.idiomatic: The Ming went further, confining examination topics to the Four Books and the Five Classics (Changes, Documents, Odes, Spring and Autumn, and Record of Rites)—essays on these themes were known as regulated exposition.

sentences.zh: 有清一沿明制，二百餘年，雖有以他途進者，終不得與科第出身者相比。

translations.literal: The Qing followed the Ming system for more than two hundred years; although some advanced by other routes, in the end they could not be compared with those who came up through the examination ranks.
translations.idiomatic: The Qing adhered to the Ming system for more than two centuries. Men who entered service by other paths might rise, but they never stood on equal footing with graduates of the civil examinations.

sentences.zh: 康、乾兩朝，特開制科。

translations.literal: In the Kangxi and Qianlong reigns, special examination categories were opened.
translations.idiomatic: Under the Kangxi and Qianlong emperors, special examination categories were instituted.

sentences.zh: 博學鴻詞，號稱得人。

translations.literal: The erudition and eminent literary composition [examinations] were acclaimed for obtaining worthy men.
translations.idiomatic: The erudition and eminent literary composition examinations were celebrated for bringing genuine talent into service.

sentences.zh: 然所試者亦僅詩、賦、策論而已。

translations.literal: Yet what was tested was also only poetry, fu, policy essays, and disquisitions.
translations.idiomatic: Even so, candidates were tested only in poetry, fu, policy essays, and disquisitions.

sentences.zh: 洎乎末造，世變日亟。

translations.literal: By the dynasty's final phase, worldly changes grew daily more urgent.
translations.idiomatic: In the dynasty's closing years, the pace of change accelerated daily.

sentences.zh: 論者謂科目人才不足應時務，毅然罷科舉，興學校。

translations.literal: Critics said that examination-curriculum talent was insufficient to meet the needs of the age, and resolutely abolished the civil examinations and established schools.
translations.idiomatic: Reformers argued that examination graduates could no longer meet the demands of the age; the examinations were abolished and modern schools established.

sentences.zh: 采東、西各國教育之新制，變唐、宋以來選舉之成規。

translations.literal: They adopted the new educational systems of Eastern and Western countries, transforming the settled norms of selection since Tang and Song.
translations.idiomatic: New educational models from East and West were adopted, overturning the selection and examination conventions that had governed China since Tang and Song times.

sentences.zh: 前後學制，判然兩事焉。

translations.literal: The educational systems before and after were clearly two different matters.
translations.idiomatic: The school systems of the earlier and later periods were altogether different institutions.

sentences.zh: 今綜其章制沿革新舊異同之故著於篇。

translations.literal: Now we summarize the regulations, their continuity and reform, and the reasons for old and new differences, and set them forth in this chapter.
translations.idiomatic: The present chapter summarizes these regulations—their continuity and reform—and records how the old and new systems diverged.

sentences.zh: 學校一

translations.literal: Schools 1.
translations.idiomatic: Schools, Part 1

sentences.zh: 有清學校，向沿明制。

translations.literal: Qing schools had long followed the Ming system.
translations.idiomatic: Qing dynasty schools followed the Ming system.

sentences.zh: 京師曰國學，並設八旗、宗室等官學。

translations.literal: In the capital it was called the National University, and banner, imperial clan, and other official schools were also established.
translations.idiomatic: In the capital the National University served as the apex institution, alongside banner schools, schools for the imperial clan, and other official academies.

sentences.zh: 直省曰府、州、縣學。

translations.literal: In the provinces directly under the capital it was called prefectural, departmental, and district schools.
translations.idiomatic: In the provinces, education was organized through prefectural, departmental, and district schools.

sentences.zh: 世祖定鼎燕京，修明北監為太學。

translations.literal: When the Shizu Emperor fixed the capital at Yanjing, he renovated the Ming Northern Directorate as the Imperial University.
translations.idiomatic: After the Shizu Emperor established the capital at Beijing, the Ming Northern Directorate was renovated as the Imperial University.

sentences.zh: 順治元年，置祭酒、司業及監丞、博士、助教、學正、學錄、典籍、典簿等官。

translations.literal: In the first year of Shunzhi, the offices of libationer, vice director, directorate assistant, erudite, instructor, study director, study recorder, archivist, and registrar were established.
translations.idiomatic: In Shunzhi 1 (1644), the posts of libationer, vice director, directorate assistant, erudite, instructor, study director, study recorder, archivist, and registrar were created.

sentences.zh: 設六堂為講肄之所，曰率性、修道、誠心、正義、崇志、廣業，一仍明舊。

translations.literal: Six halls were set up as places for lecturing and study, called Following Nature, Cultivating the Way, Sincere Heart, Correct Righteousness, Honoring Aspiration, and Broadening Enterprise—altogether following Ming precedent.
translations.idiomatic: Six lecture halls were established for instruction and study—Following Nature, Cultivating the Way, Sincere Heart, Correct Righteousness, Honoring Aspiration, and Broadening Enterprise—retaining Ming nomenclature.

sentences.zh: 少詹事李若琳首為祭酒，請仿明初制，廣收生徒，官生除恩廕外，七品以上官子弟勤敏好學者，民生除貢生外，廩、增、附生員文義優長者，並許提學考選送監。

translations.literal: Junior Mentor of the Heir Apparent Li Ruolin was the first libationer; he requested following the early Ming system to broadly enroll students: for official students, aside from grace enfeoffment, sons of officials of the seventh rank and above who were diligent, keen, and fond of learning; for common students, aside from tribute students, stipendiary, augmented, and attached licentiates outstanding in literary meaning—all were permitted to be examined and selected by the education intendant and sent to the Directorate.
translations.idiomatic: Li Ruolin, Junior Mentor of the Heir Apparent, became the first libationer. He petitioned to follow the early Ming model and broaden enrollment: official students included, beyond grace enfeoffment cases, sons of seventh-rank officials and above who were diligent and studious; common students included, beyond tribute graduates, stipendiary, augmented, and attached licentiates of superior literary attainment—all to be examined by the provincial education intendant and sent to the Directorate.

sentences.zh: 又言學以國子名，所謂國之貴遊子弟學焉。

translations.literal: He also said that the school is named for the heir of the state—meaning that the noble scions of the state study there.
translations.idiomatic: He noted that the institution's name, guozi, signified that the sons of the state's elite were to study there.

sentences.zh: 前朝公、侯、伯、駙馬初襲授者，皆入國學讀書。

translations.literal: In the previous dynasty, those who first received investiture as duke, marquis, earl, or imperial son-in-law all entered the National University to study.
translations.idiomatic: Under the previous dynasty, newly invested dukes, marquises, earls, and imperial sons-in-law all entered the National University to study.

sentences.zh: 滿洲勛臣子弟有志向學者，並請送監肄業。

translations.literal: Sons of Manchu meritorious ministers who aspired to study were also requested to be sent to the Directorate for study.
translations.idiomatic: He also asked that sons of Manchu meritorious officials who wished to study be sent to the Directorate.

sentences.zh: 詔允增設滿洲司業、助教等官，是為八旗子弟入監之始。

translations.literal: An edict approved adding Manchu vice directors, instructors, and other officials—this was the beginning of Eight Banner youths entering the Directorate.
translations.idiomatic: The throne approved additional Manchu vice directors and instructors—marking the beginning of Eight Banner students' enrollment at the Directorate.

sentences.zh: 厥後定為限制，條例屢更，益臻詳備。

translations.literal: Thereafter limits were fixed, regulations were repeatedly revised, and the system grew ever more detailed and complete.
translations.idiomatic: Subsequently enrollment was restricted, regulations revised repeatedly, until the system grew increasingly detailed.

sentences.zh: 肄業生徒，有貢、有監。

translations.literal: Students pursuing study were of two kinds: tribute and directorate.
translations.idiomatic: Students at the Directorate fell into two categories: tribute students and directorate students.

sentences.zh: 貢生凡六：曰歲貢、恩貢、拔貢、優貢、副貢、例貢。

translations.literal: Tribute students numbered six kinds: called annual tribute, grace tribute, selected tribute, superior tribute, supplementary tribute, and quota tribute.
translations.idiomatic: There were six types of tribute student: annual, grace, selected, superior, supplementary, and quota tribute.

sentences.zh: 監生凡四：曰恩監、廕監、優監、例監。

translations.literal: Directorate students numbered four kinds: called grace directorate, enfeoffment directorate, superior directorate, and quota directorate.
translations.idiomatic: There were four types of directorate student: grace, enfeoffment, superior, and quota directorate students.

sentences.zh: 廕監有二：曰恩廕、難廕。

translations.literal: Enfeoffment directorate students had two kinds: called grace enfeoffment and hardship enfeoffment.
translations.idiomatic: Enfeoffment directorate students were of two types: grace enfeoffment and hardship enfeoffment.

sentences.zh: 通謂之國子監生。

translations.literal: Collectively they were called Imperial University students.
translations.idiomatic: All were known collectively as Imperial University students.

sentences.zh: 六堂肄業，分內、外班。

translations.literal: Study in the six halls was divided into inner and outer classes.
translations.idiomatic: Students in the six halls were divided into inner and outer classes.

sentences.zh: 初，內班百五十名，堂各二十五名；

translations.literal: At first the inner class had one hundred fifty names, twenty-five per hall;
translations.idiomatic: Initially the inner class numbered one hundred fifty, twenty-five per hall;

sentences.zh: 外班百二十名，堂各二十名。

translations.literal: the outer class one hundred twenty names, twenty per hall.
translations.idiomatic: the outer class one hundred twenty, twenty per hall.

sentences.zh: 戶部歲發帑銀，給膏火，獎勵有差，餘備周恤。

translations.literal: The Ministry of Revenue annually disbursed treasury silver for lamp oil and study stipends, with graded rewards, the remainder reserved for relief.
translations.idiomatic: The Ministry of Revenue disbursed annual stipends for lamp oil and study expenses, with graded rewards; surplus funds covered emergency relief.

sentences.zh: 乾隆初，改內班堂各三十名，內、外共三百名。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Qianlong, the inner class was changed to thirty per hall, inner and outer totaling three hundred.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Qianlong reign, the inner class was raised to thirty per hall, three hundred inner and outer combined.

sentences.zh: 既而裁外班百二十名，加內班膏火，撥內班二十四名為外班。

translations.literal: Thereafter the outer class of one hundred twenty was cut, inner-class stipends were increased, and twenty-four inner-class places were reassigned as outer class.
translations.idiomatic: The outer class of one hundred twenty was then abolished, inner-class stipends increased, and twenty-four inner-class places reassigned to the outer class.

sentences.zh: 嘉慶初，以八旗及大、宛兩縣肄業生距家近，不住舍，不許補內班。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Jiaqing, because Eight Banner students and students from Daxing and Wanping counties lived near home and did not lodge in the dormitories, they were not permitted to fill inner-class vacancies.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Jiaqing, Eight Banner students and those from Daxing and Wanping counties, living near home and not residing in dormitories, were barred from promotion to the inner class.

sentences.zh: 補班之始，赴監應試，曰考到。

translations.literal: At the beginning of filling a class vacancy, one went to the Directorate to sit for examination—called kao dao.
translations.idiomatic: To fill a class vacancy, students first presented themselves at the Directorate for examination—the kao dao.

sentences.zh: 列一、二等者再試，曰考驗。

translations.literal: Those ranked first or second class were examined again—called kao yan.
translations.idiomatic: Those placed in the first or second rank underwent a second examination—the kao yan.

sentences.zh: 貢生一、二等，監生一等，乃許肄業。

translations.literal: Tribute students of first or second class, directorate students of first class, were then permitted to pursue study.
translations.idiomatic: Only tribute students in the first or second rank, or directorate students in the first rank, were permitted to enroll for study.

sentences.zh: 假滿回監曰復班。

translations.literal: When leave expired and one returned to the Directorate, it was called fu ban.
translations.idiomatic: Return after leave expired was termed fu ban.

sentences.zh: 內班生原依親處館，滿、蒙、漢軍恩監生習繙譯或騎射，不能竟月在學者，改外班。

translations.literal: Inner-class students originally lodged with relatives; Manchu, Mongol, and Han Banner grace directorate students studying translation or archery and horsemanship who could not remain at school for the full month were transferred to the outer class.
translations.idiomatic: Inner-class students often lodged with relatives; Manchu, Mongol, and Han Banner grace directorate students training in translation or archery who could not attend for the full month were reassigned to the outer class.

sentences.zh: 曠大課一次，無故離學至三次以上，例罰改外。

translations.literal: Missing one major examination, or leaving school without cause three times or more, by regulation incurred demotion to the outer class.
translations.idiomatic: Missing one major examination, or absenting oneself without cause three or more times, carried demotion to the outer class by regulation.

sentences.zh: 置集愆冊，治諸不帥教者。

translations.literal: A register of accumulated faults was kept to discipline those who did not follow instruction.
translations.idiomatic: A register of accumulated faults disciplined students who failed to follow instruction.

sentences.zh: 出入必記於簿，監丞掌之。

translations.literal: Entries and exits had to be recorded in a ledger, kept by the directorate assistant.
translations.idiomatic: All comings and goings were recorded in a ledger maintained by the directorate assistant.

sentences.zh: 省親、完姻、丁憂、告病及同居伯、叔、兄長喪而無子者，予假歸里，限期回監。

translations.literal: Visiting parents, completing marriage, mourning for parents, reporting illness, and cases where a co-resident uncle, elder brother, or senior brother died without a son—leave to return home was granted, with a fixed term to return to the Directorate.
translations.idiomatic: Leave was granted to visit parents, complete marriage, observe mourning, report illness, or when a co-resident uncle or elder brother died childless; students were required to return by a fixed deadline.

sentences.zh: 遲誤懲罰，私歸黜革，冒替除名。

translations.literal: Delay incurred punishment; unauthorized return led to dismissal; impersonation led to removal of name.
translations.idiomatic: Late return brought punishment; unauthorized departure meant dismissal; impersonation meant expulsion.

sentences.zh: 課士之法，月朔、望釋奠畢，博士廳集諸生，講解經書。

translations.literal: The method of examining scholars: on the first and fifteenth of the month, after the libation ceremony, the erudite's hall assembled all students to lecture on and explain the classics.
translations.idiomatic: Examination of students proceeded as follows: on the first and fifteenth of each month, after the libation ceremony, the erudite assembled students in the lecture hall to expound the classics.

sentences.zh: 上旬助教講義。

translations.literal: In the first ten days of the month the instructor lectured on meaning.
translations.idiomatic: During the first ten days of the month, instructors delivered lectures on textual meaning.

sentences.zh: 既望，學正、學錄講書各一次。

translations.literal: After the full moon, the study director and study recorder each lectured on the books once.
translations.idiomatic: After the full moon, the study director and study recorder each lectured once.

sentences.zh: 會講、覆講、上書、覆背，月三回，周而復始。

translations.literal: Joint lecture, review lecture, presenting writing, and reciting from memory—three times per month, cycling repeatedly.
translations.idiomatic: Joint lectures, review lectures, written presentations, and recitations from memory occurred three times monthly in rotation.

sentences.zh: 所習四書、五經、性理、通鑒諸書，其兼通十三經、二十一史，博極群書者，隨資學所詣。

translations.literal: What was studied were the Four Books, Five Classics, Nature and Principle, Comprehensive Mirror, and such works; those who also mastered the Thirteen Classics, Twenty-one Histories, and exhaustively probed all books advanced according to the reach of their learning.
translations.idiomatic: Core curriculum comprised the Four Books, Five Classics, Nature and Principle, and Comprehensive Mirror; students who mastered the Thirteen Classics, Twenty-one Histories, or broader learning advanced according to their attainment.

sentences.zh: 日摹晉、唐名帖數百字，立日課冊，旬日呈助教等批晰，朔、望呈堂查驗。

translations.literal: Daily they copied several hundred characters from famous Jin and Tang model calligraphy, kept a daily lesson register, presented it every ten days to instructors for marking, and on the first and fifteenth presented it to the hall for inspection.
translations.idiomatic: Students copied several hundred characters daily from Jin and Tang model calligraphy, recorded progress in a daily lesson book, submitted it to instructors every ten days for correction, and presented it to the hall on the first and fifteenth for inspection.

sentences.zh: 祭酒、司業月望輪課四書文一、詩一，曰大課。

translations.literal: Libationer and vice director on the fifteenth of the month in rotation examined one Four Books essay and one poem—called the major examination.
translations.idiomatic: On the fifteenth of each month, libationer and vice director alternated in examining one Four Books essay and one poem—the major examination.

sentences.zh: 祭酒季考，司業月課，皆用四書、五經文，並詔、誥、表、策論、判。

translations.literal: The libationer's quarterly examination and the vice director's monthly examination all used Four Books and Five Classics essays, together with edicts, announcements, memorials, policy essays, and legal judgments.
translations.idiomatic: The libationer's quarterly and vice director's monthly examinations required Four Books and Five Classics essays, plus edicts, announcements, memorials, policy essays, and legal judgments.

sentences.zh: 月朔，博士廳課經文、經解及策論。

translations.literal: On the first of the month, the erudite's hall examined classic texts, classic exegesis, and policy essays.
translations.idiomatic: On the first of each month, the erudite's hall examined classic texts, exegesis, and policy essays.

sentences.zh: 月三日，助教課，十八日，學正、學錄課，各試四書文一、詩一、經文或策一。

translations.literal: On the third of the month the instructor examined; on the eighteenth the study director and study recorder examined—each testing one Four Books essay, one poem, and one classic text or policy essay.
translations.idiomatic: On the third, instructors examined students; on the eighteenth, study directors and recorders did so—each session requiring one Four Books essay, one poem, and one classic text or policy essay.

sentences.zh: 積分歷事之法，國初行之。

translations.literal: The method of accumulating points and serving in departments was practiced in the early dynasty.
translations.idiomatic: The point-accumulation and departmental service system was practiced in the early dynasty.

sentences.zh: 監生坐監期滿，撥歷部院練習政體。

translations.literal: When directorate students completed their term of residence, they were assigned to serve in ministries and courts to practice the forms of government.
translations.idiomatic: Upon completing residence, directorate students were assigned to ministries and courts to learn administrative practice.

sentences.zh: 三月考勤，一年期滿送廷試。

translations.literal: After three months' attendance check, when the one-year term was complete they were sent to the palace examination.
translations.idiomatic: After three months of attendance verification and one year of service, they were sent to the palace examination.

sentences.zh: 其免坐監，或免歷一月二月者，恩詔有之，非常例也。

translations.literal: Exemption from residence, or exemption from one or two months of service, occurred under grace edicts and was not the regular rule.
translations.idiomatic: Exemptions from residence or from one or two months of service were granted by special edict, not as regular practice.

sentences.zh: 順治三年，祭酒薛所蘊奏定漢監生積分法，常課外，月試經義、策論各一，合式者拔置一等。

translations.literal: In Shunzhi 3, Libationer Xue Suoyun memorialized fixing the point-accumulation method for Han directorate students: beyond regular lessons, monthly tests of classic meaning and policy essays one each; those meeting the standard were selected for first class.
translations.idiomatic: In Shunzhi 3 (1646), Libationer Xue Suoyun established the point system for Han directorate students: beyond regular coursework, monthly tests in classic meaning and policy essays; those passing were ranked first class.

sentences.zh: 歲考一等十二次為及格，免撥歷，送廷試超選。

translations.literal: Twelve first-class results in the annual examination counted as passing; exemption from assigned service, sent to the palace examination for super-selection.
translations.idiomatic: Twelve first-class annual results constituted a passing grade, exempting students from departmental service and qualifying them for preferential selection at the palace examination.

sentences.zh: 十五年，祭酒固爾嘉渾議：「令監生考到日，拔其尤者許積分；

translations.literal: In year 15, Libationer Gu'erjia Hun proposed: "Let directorate students on the day of kao dao select the most outstanding to be permitted to accumulate points;
translations.idiomatic: In Shunzhi 15 (1658), Libationer Gu'erjia Hun proposed: "On the kao dao examination day, select the most outstanding directorate students for point accumulation;

sentences.zh: 不與者，期滿咨部歷事。

translations.literal: those not granted it, when the term expired, were referred to the ministry for service.
translations.idiomatic: those not selected would, upon completing their term, be referred to ministries for service.

sentences.zh: 積分法一年為限。

translations.literal: The point method had a limit of one year.
translations.idiomatic: Point accumulation was limited to one year.

sentences.zh: 常課外，月試一等與一分，二等半分，二等以下無分。

translations.literal: Beyond regular lessons, monthly tests: first class received one point, second class half a point, below second class no points.
translations.idiomatic: Beyond regular lessons, monthly examinations awarded one point for first class, half a point for second class, and none below second class.

sentences.zh: 有五經兼通，全史精熟，或善摹鍾、王諸帖，雖文不及格，亦與一分。

translations.literal: Those who mastered all Five Classics, were thoroughly versed in the complete histories, or excelled at copying Zhong and Wang model calligraphy—even if their essays did not pass, still received one point.
translations.idiomatic: Students who mastered all Five Classics, knew the complete histories thoroughly, or excelled at copying Zhong and Wang calligraphy received one point even if their essays failed.

sentences.zh: 積滿八分為及格，歲不逾十餘人。

translations.literal: Accumulating eight full points counted as passing; each year no more than a dozen or so persons.
translations.idiomatic: Eight points constituted a passing grade; fewer than a dozen students achieved this annually.

sentences.zh: 恩、拔、歲、副，咨部歷滿考職，照教習貢生例，上上卷用通判，上卷用知縣。

translations.literal: Grace, selected, annual, and supplementary tribute students, when service was complete, were referred to the ministry for office examination; following the teaching-assistant tribute student precedent, top-top rolls received subprefect, top rolls received magistrate.
translations.idiomatic: Grace, selected, annual, and supplementary tribute students, upon completing service, took the office examination; following teaching-assistant precedent, top-top rolls received subprefect posts, top rolls magistracies.

sentences.zh: 例監歷滿考職，與不積分貢生一體廷試。

translations.literal: Quota directorate students, when service was complete, took the office examination together with tribute students who had not accumulated points, all in one palace examination.
translations.idiomatic: Quota directorate students and tribute students without accumulated points took the office examination together at the palace examination.

sentences.zh: 每百名取正印八名，餘用州、縣佐貳。

translations.literal: Of every hundred, eight principal seals were taken; the remainder were used as prefectural and district assistants.
translations.idiomatic: Of every hundred candidates, eight received principal appointments; the remainder filled prefectural and district assistant posts.

sentences.zh: 積分不滿數，原分部者，咨部不得優選。

translations.literal: Those whose points did not reach the number, originally assigned to departments, when referred to the ministry could not receive preferential selection.
translations.idiomatic: Students with insufficient points, though originally assigned to departments, could not receive preferential selection when referred to the ministry.

sentences.zh: 原再肄業滿分者聽。」

translations.literal: Those who wished to study again until full points were permitted."
translations.idiomatic: They might return to study until accumulating full points if they wished."

sentences.zh: 從之。

translations.literal: Approval followed.
translations.idiomatic: The proposal was approved.

sentences.zh: 是年，科臣王命岳以貢途壅塞，請暫停恩、拔、歲貢。

translations.literal: That year, Censor Wang Mingyue, because the tribute route was congested, requested temporarily suspending grace, selected, and annual tribute.
translations.idiomatic: That year, Censor Wang Mingyue, citing congestion in the tribute pipeline, petitioned to suspend grace, selected, and annual tribute temporarily.

sentences.zh: 於是坐監人少，難較分數。

translations.literal: Thus those residing at the Directorate were few, and it was difficult to compare scores.
translations.idiomatic: Resident students became scarce, making point comparison impractical.

sentences.zh: 十七年，固爾嘉渾奏停積分法，後遂不復行。

translations.literal: In year 17, Gu'erjia Hun memorialized stopping the point method; thereafter it was never practiced again.
translations.idiomatic: In Shunzhi 17 (1660), Gu'erjia Hun memorialized to abolish the point system, which was never revived.

sentences.zh: 康熙初，並停撥歷，期滿咨部考試，用州同、州判、縣丞、主簿、吏目。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Kangxi, assignment to service was also stopped; when the term expired they were referred to the ministry for examination and used as subprefect, subprefect judge, assistant magistrate, registrar, and clerk.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Kangxi, departmental assignments ceased; upon completing residence, students took the ministry examination and were appointed subprefect, subprefect judge, assistant magistrate, registrar, or clerk.

sentences.zh: 自是部院諸司無監生，惟考選通文理能楷書者，送修書各館，較年勞議敘，照應得職銜選用，優者或加等焉。

translations.literal: From this time ministries and courts had no directorate students; only those examined and selected as versed in literary principles and able in regular script were sent to the various compilation bureaus; years of labor were compared to deliberate appointment, and according to the office title due they were selected for use; the superior sometimes received added rank.
translations.idiomatic: Thereafter ministries and courts no longer received directorate students; only those proficient in literary studies and regular script were sent to compilation bureaus, where years of service determined appointment according to earned rank, with outstanding performers sometimes promoted.

sentences.zh: 監生坐監期，恩貢六月，歲貢八月，副貢廩膳六月，增、附八月，拔貢廩膳十四月，增、附十六月，恩廕二十四月，難廕六月，例貢廩膳十四月，增、附十六月，俊秀二十四月。

translations.literal: Directorate students' term of residence: grace tribute six months, annual tribute eight months, supplementary tribute stipendiary six months, augmented and attached eight months, selected tribute stipendiary fourteen months, augmented and attached sixteen months, grace enfeoffment twenty-four months, hardship enfeoffment six months, quota tribute stipendiary fourteen months, augmented and attached sixteen months, talented youth twenty-four months.
translations.idiomatic: Residence terms varied: grace tribute six months, annual tribute eight; supplementary tribute stipendiary six, augmented and attached eight; selected tribute stipendiary fourteen, augmented and attached sixteen; grace enfeoffment twenty-four, hardship enfeoffment six; quota tribute stipendiary fourteen, augmented and attached sixteen; talented youth twenty-four.

sentences.zh: 例監計捐監月分三十六月。

translations.literal: Quota directorate students, counting donation directorate months, thirty-six months.
translations.idiomatic: Quota directorate students, including purchased enrollment, served thirty-six months.

sentences.zh: 雍正五年，定除監期計算。

translations.literal: In Yongzheng 5, it was fixed to calculate excluding the residence term.
translations.idiomatic: In Yongzheng 5 (1727), calculation excluding the residence term was standardized.

sentences.zh: 各監生肄業，率以連閏扣滿三年為期。

translations.literal: All directorate students pursuing study generally took three years counting intercalary months as the term.
translations.idiomatic: All directorate students generally completed three years of study, intercalary months included.

sentences.zh: 告假、丁憂、考劣、記過，則扣除月日。

translations.literal: Leave, mourning, poor examination results, and recorded demerits—then months and days were deducted.
translations.idiomatic: Leave, mourning, poor examination results, and recorded demerits extended the term by deducting corresponding time.

sentences.zh: 告假依限到監，或逾限而本籍有司官具牘者，仍前後通算。

translations.literal: Those on leave who returned within the limit, or exceeded the limit but whose home-district officials submitted documents, still had before and after calculated together.
translations.idiomatic: Students returning within the leave limit, or late with documentation from home officials, had time counted continuously.

sentences.zh: 舊制，祭酒、司業總理監務。

translations.literal: Under the old system, libationer and vice director jointly managed directorate affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Under the old system, libationer and vice director jointly administered the Directorate.

sentences.zh: 雍正三年，始設管理監事大臣。

translations.literal: In Yongzheng 3, the post of supervising minister for directorate affairs was first established.
translations.idiomatic: In Yongzheng 3 (1725), a supervising minister for Directorate affairs was first appointed.

sentences.zh: 乾隆二年，孫嘉淦以刑部尚書管監事。

translations.literal: In Qianlong 2, Sun Jiagan as Minister of Justice supervised directorate affairs.
translations.idiomatic: In Qianlong 2 (1737), Sun Jiagan, Minister of Justice, supervised Directorate affairs.

sentences.zh: 初嘉淦在世宗朝官司業，奏言：「學校之教，宜先經術，請敕天下學臣，選拔諸生貢太學，九卿舉經明行修之士為助教，一以經術造士。

translations.literal: Earlier, when Jiagan in the Shizong reign was vice director, he memorialized: "School teaching should put classic learning first; we request ordering education officials throughout the realm to select and send licentiates as tribute to the Imperial University, and the Nine Ministers to recommend men clear in the classics and cultivated in conduct as instructors—altogether to form scholars through classic learning.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, as vice director under the Shizong Emperor, Sun Jiagan memorialized: "School instruction should prioritize classical learning. I request that education officials throughout the realm select licentiates for the Imperial University, and that the Nine Ministers recommend scholars distinguished in classics and conduct as instructors—to cultivate talent through classical studies alone.

sentences.zh: 三年考成，舉以待用。」

translations.literal: After three years examine achievement, recommend them to await employment."
translations.idiomatic: After three years, examine their achievement and recommend them for appointment."

sentences.zh: 議未及行，遷祭酒，申前請，世宗韙之。

translations.literal: The proposal had not yet been implemented when he was transferred to libationer; he renewed his former request, and the Shizong Emperor approved it.
translations.idiomatic: Before the proposal could be implemented, he was promoted to libationer and renewed his petition; the Shizong Emperor approved.

sentences.zh: 先是太學生名為坐監肄業，率假館散處。

translations.literal: Previously Imperial University students were nominally resident for study, but mostly lodged elsewhere scattered about.
translations.idiomatic: Previously, Imperial University students were nominally in residence but mostly lodged elsewhere.

sentences.zh: 遇釋奠、堂期、季考、月課，暫一齊集。

translations.literal: When libation ceremonies, hall sessions, quarterly examinations, or monthly lessons occurred, they briefly assembled together.
translations.idiomatic: They assembled only for libation ceremonies, hall sessions, quarterly examinations, and monthly lessons.

sentences.zh: 監內舊有號房五百餘間，修圮不時，且資斧不給，無以宿諸生。

translations.literal: Within the Directorate there had been more than five hundred numbered rooms; repairs were not timely, and moreover funds were insufficient, so there was no lodging for students.
translations.idiomatic: The Directorate's five hundred numbered rooms had fallen into disrepair for lack of funds, leaving no lodging for students.

sentences.zh: 嘉淦言：「各省拔貢雲集京師，需住監者三百餘人。

translations.literal: Jiagan said: "Selected tribute students from all provinces gather at the capital; more than three hundred need to lodge at the Directorate.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Jiagan reported: "Selected tribute students from all provinces gather in the capital; more than three hundred require Directorate lodging.

sentences.zh: 六堂祗可誦讀，不能棲止。

translations.literal: The six halls can only be used for recitation and study, not for dwelling.
translations.idiomatic: The six halls serve only for study, not residence.

sentences.zh: 乞給監南官房，令助教等官及肄業生居住。

translations.literal: We beg allocation of official quarters south of the Directorate, to let instructors and students pursuing study reside there.
translations.idiomatic: I request official quarters south of the Directorate for instructors and resident students.

sentences.zh: 歲給銀六千兩為講課、桌飯、衣服、賑助之費。」

translations.literal: Six thousand taels of silver were granted annually for lecture fees, table meals, clothing, and relief expenses."
translations.idiomatic: Six thousand taels of silver were allocated annually for lectures, board, clothing, and student relief."

sentences.zh: 允之。

translations.literal: Approval was granted.
translations.idiomatic: The request was approved.

sentences.zh: 是為南學。

translations.literal: This was the Southern Academy.
translations.idiomatic: This became known as the Southern Academy.

sentences.zh: 至是，請仿宋儒胡瑗經義、治事分齋遺法。

translations.literal: At this point he requested following the legacy method of the Song Confucian Hu Yuan's separate halls for classic meaning and practical administration.
translations.idiomatic: He then petitioned to revive the Song Confucian Hu Yuan's method of separate halls for classical studies and practical administration.

sentences.zh: 明經者，或治一經，或兼他經，務取御纂折中、傳說諸書，探其原本，講明人倫日用之理。

translations.literal: Those clarifying the classics might specialize in one classic or combine others; they were to take the imperially compiled balanced texts and transmitted exegeses, probe their originals, and expound the principles of human relations and daily use.
translations.idiomatic: Students of the classics might specialize in one classic or study several, drawing on imperially authorized commentaries and transmitted exegeses to expound the moral principles governing daily life.

sentences.zh: 治事者，如歷代典禮、賦役、律令、邊防、水利、天官、河渠、算法之類。

translations.literal: Those administering affairs studied such subjects as ritual institutions through the ages, taxation and corvée, statutes, frontier defense, water control, celestial offices, river works, and calculation.
translations.idiomatic: Students of practical administration studied ritual institutions, taxation and corvée, law, frontier defense, hydraulic engineering, astronomy, river management, and mathematics.

sentences.zh: 或專治一事，或兼治數事，務窮究其源流利弊。

translations.literal: Some specialized in one matter, others combined several; the task was to exhaustively investigate origins, currents, benefits, and harms.
translations.idiomatic: Some specialized in a single subject, others in several, all seeking thorough understanding of origins, practice, benefits, and abuses.

sentences.zh: 考試時，必以經術湛深、通達事理、驗稽古愛民之識。

translations.literal: At examination time, depth in classic learning, mastery of affairs and principles, and proof of antiquity-examining, people-loving insight were required.
translations.idiomatic: Examinations required deep classical learning, practical understanding of governance, and demonstrated commitment to historical learning and care for the people.

sentences.zh: 三年期滿，分別等第，以示勸懲。

translations.literal: When the three-year term was complete, grades were distinguished to show encouragement and punishment.
translations.idiomatic: After three years, students were ranked to reward achievement and discipline failure.

sentences.zh: 從之。

translations.literal: Approval followed.
translations.idiomatic: The proposal was approved.

sentences.zh: 令諸生有心得或疑義，逐條劄記，呈助教批判，按期呈堂。

translations.literal: Students with insights or doubts were ordered to record them item by item, present them to instructors for critique, and on schedule present them to the hall.
translations.idiomatic: Students recorded insights and questions item by item for instructor critique, then submitted them to the hall on schedule.

sentences.zh: 季考月課，改四書題一，五經講義題各一，治事策問一。

translations.literal: Quarterly and monthly examinations were changed to one Four Books topic, one exegesis topic for each of the Five Classics, and one policy question on practical administration.
translations.idiomatic: Quarterly and monthly examinations were revised to require one Four Books essay, one exegesis essay per classic, and one policy question on practical administration.

sentences.zh: 時高宗加意太學，嘉淦嚴立課程，獎誘備至，六堂講師，極一時之選。

translations.literal: At this time the Gaozong Emperor paid special attention to the Imperial University; Jiagan strictly established the curriculum and rewarded and encouraged to the utmost; the six halls' lecturers were the finest selection of the age.
translations.idiomatic: The Gaozong Emperor lavished attention on the Imperial University. Sun Jiagan enforced a rigorous curriculum with generous rewards; the six halls' lecturers were the finest scholars of the age.

sentences.zh: 舉人吳鼎、梁錫興，皆以薦舉經學授司業。

translations.literal: Juren Wu Ding and Liang Xixing were both appointed vice directors through recommendation for classical learning.
translations.idiomatic: Juren Wu Ding and Liang Xixing were appointed vice directors on recommendation for their classical scholarship.

sentences.zh: 進士庄亨陽，舉人潘永季、蔡德峻、秦蕙田、吳鼐，貢生官獻瑤、王文震，監生夏宗瀾，皆以潛心經學，先後被薦為本監屬官。

translations.literal: Jinshi Zhuang Hengyang, juren Pan Yongji, Cai Dejun, Qin Huitian, and Wu Nai, tribute student Guan Xianyao and Wang Wenzhen, and directorate student Xia Zonglan—all because of devoted classical learning—were successively recommended as subordinate officials of this Directorate.
translations.idiomatic: Jinshi Zhuang Hengyang; juren Pan Yongji, Cai Dejun, Qin Huitian, and Wu Nai; tribute students Guan Xianyao and Wang Wenzhen; and directorate student Xia Zonglan—all distinguished classical scholars—were successively appointed Directorate officials.

sentences.zh: 分長六堂，各佔一經，時有「四賢五君子」之稱。

translations.literal: They divided leadership of the six halls, each holding one classic; at the time they were called the "Four Worthies and Five Gentlemen."
translations.idiomatic: They headed the six halls, each presiding over one classic, and were known as the "Four Worthies and Five Gentlemen."

sentences.zh: 師徒濟濟，皆奮自鏃礪，研求實學。

translations.literal: Teachers and students abounded; all exerted themselves to hone and polish, researching practical learning.
translations.idiomatic: Teachers and students flourished together, all striving to pursue genuine learning.

sentences.zh: 而祭酒趙國麟又以經義、治事外，應講習時藝，請頒六堂欽定四書文資誦習。

translations.literal: Libationer Zhao Guolin further held that beyond classic meaning and practical administration, contemporary examination arts should be studied; he requested distributing the six halls' imperially approved Four Books essays for recitation and study.
translations.idiomatic: Libationer Zhao Guolin argued that beyond classical and practical studies, students should practice examination essays, and petitioned to distribute imperially approved Four Books model essays for study.

sentences.zh: 並報可。

translations.literal: This too was reported approved.
translations.idiomatic: This too was approved.

sentences.zh: 清代臨雍視學典禮綦重。

translations.literal: The Qing dynasty's ceremony of the emperor's presence at the Imperial Academy to inspect learning was exceedingly weighty.
translations.idiomatic: The Qing placed enormous weight on the emperor's ceremony of inspecting learning at the Imperial Academy.

sentences.zh: 順治九年，世祖首視學。

translations.literal: In Shunzhi 9, the Shizu Emperor first inspected learning.
translations.idiomatic: In Shunzhi 9 (1652), the Shizu Emperor first performed the learning inspection.

sentences.zh: 先期行取衍聖公、五經博士率孔氏暨先賢各氏族裔赴京觀禮。

translations.literal: In advance the Duke Who Extends Sageliness, the Five Classics doctors, leading Kong clansmen and descendants of various sages' lineages, were summoned to the capital to observe the ceremony.
translations.idiomatic: The Duke Who Extends Sageliness, Five Classics doctors, and descendants of Confucius and other sages were summoned to the capital in advance to witness the ceremony.

sentences.zh: 帝釋奠畢，詣彝倫堂御講幄。

translations.literal: When the Emperor had completed the libation sacrifice, he proceeded to the Hall of Human Relations imperial lecture pavilion.
translations.idiomatic: After completing the libation sacrifice, the emperor proceeded to the imperial lecture pavilion in the Hall of Human Relations.

sentences.zh: 祭酒講四書，司業講經。

translations.literal: The libationer lectured on the Four Books; the vice director lectured on the classics.
translations.idiomatic: The libationer lectured on the Four Books; the vice director on the classics.

sentences.zh: 宣制勉太學諸生。

translations.literal: An edict was proclaimed to encourage Imperial University students.
translations.idiomatic: An edict was proclaimed exhorting the university students.

sentences.zh: 越日，賜衍聖公冠服，國子監官賞賚有差。

translations.literal: The next day, the Duke Who Extends Sageliness was granted cap and robes; Imperial University officials received graded rewards.
translations.idiomatic: The following day, the Duke Who Extends Sageliness received ceremonial robes; Directorate officials received graded rewards.

sentences.zh: 各氏後裔送監讀書。

translations.literal: Descendants of the various lineages were sent to the Directorate to study.
translations.idiomatic: Descendants of the sage lineages were sent to study at the Directorate.

sentences.zh: 嗣是歷代舉行以為常。

translations.literal: Thereafter successive generations held it as regular practice.
translations.idiomatic: Subsequent emperors made this a regular practice.

sentences.zh: 乾隆四十八年諭曰：「稽古國學之制，天子曰辟雍，所以行禮樂、宣德化、昭文明而流教澤，典至鉅也。

translations.literal: In Qianlong 48 an edict said: "Examining antiquity, the National University system—the Son of Heaven's called piyong—is for performing ritual and music, spreading virtuous transformation, displaying civilization and flowing educational grace; the canon is supremely great.
translations.idiomatic: In Qianlong 48 (1783) an edict declared: "The ancient National University system—the Son of Heaven's piyong—exists to perform ritual and music, spread moral transformation, display civilization, and extend educational grace. Its significance is paramount.

sentences.zh: 國學為人文薈萃之地，規制宜隆。

translations.literal: The National University is a place where humanistic talent gathers; its regulations should be elevated.
translations.idiomatic: The National University gathers the realm's finest scholars; its institutions should be commensurately grand.

sentences.zh: 辟雍之立，元、明以來，典尚闕如，應增建以臻美備。」

translations.literal: The establishment of piyong—from Yuan and Ming onward the canon still lacked; it should be newly built to reach perfect completeness."
translations.idiomatic: The piyong hall had been absent since Yuan and Ming times; it should be rebuilt to complete the institution."

sentences.zh: 命尚書德保，尚書兼管國子監事劉墉，侍郎德成，仿禮經舊制，於彝倫堂南營建。

translations.literal: Ministers Debao, Liu Yong who also supervised directorate affairs, and Vice Minister Decheng were ordered, following the Rites' old system, to construct it south of the Hall of Human Relations.
translations.idiomatic: Ministers Debao and Liu Yong, the latter also supervising Directorate affairs, and Vice Minister Decheng were ordered to build it south of the Hall of Human Relations according to classical ritual specifications.

sentences.zh: 明年，落成。

translations.literal: The next year it was completed.
translations.idiomatic: It was completed the following year.

sentences.zh: 又明年，高宗駕臨辟雍行講學禮。

translations.literal: The year after, the Gaozong Emperor personally arrived at piyong to perform the lecture ceremony.
translations.idiomatic: The year after, the Gaozong Emperor personally presided over the lecture ceremony at the piyong.

sentences.zh: 命大學士、伯伍彌泰，大學士管監事蔡新，進講四書。

translations.literal: Grand Secretary and Earl Wu Mitai, and Grand Secretary supervising directorate affairs Cai Xin, were ordered to advance and lecture on the Four Books.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Secretary and Earl Wu Mitai and Grand Secretary Cai Xin, who supervised Directorate affairs, lectured on the Four Books.

sentences.zh: 祭酒覺羅吉善、鄒奕孝，進講周易。

translations.literal: Libationers Janggiya Jishan and Zou Yixiao advanced and lectured on the Book of Changes.
translations.idiomatic: Libationers Janggiya Jishan and Zou Yixiao lectured on the Book of Changes.

sentences.zh: 頒御論二篇，宣示義蘊。

translations.literal: Two imperial disquisitions were issued, proclaiming their meaning and profundity.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor issued two imperial essays expounding their meaning.

sentences.zh: 王、公、衍聖公、大學士以下官，暨肄業觀禮諸生，三千八十八人，圜橋聽講。

translations.literal: Princes, dukes, the Duke Who Extends Sageliness, grand secretaries and officials below, together with students pursuing study who observed the ceremony—three thousand eighty-eight persons—listened to the lecture around the bridge.
translations.idiomatic: Three thousand eighty-eight princes, dukes, the Duke Who Extends Sageliness, grand secretaries, officials, and students gathered around the bridge to hear the lecture.

sentences.zh: 禮成，賜燕禮部，恩賚有加。

translations.literal: When the ceremony was complete, a banquet was granted at the Ministry of Rites, with added grace rewards.
translations.idiomatic: After the ceremony, a banquet was held at the Ministry of Rites with generous rewards.

sentences.zh: 是時天子右文，群臣躬遇休明，翊贊文化，彬彬稱極盛矣。

translations.literal: At this time the Son of Heaven honored literature; the multitude of ministers personally encountered a flourishing and enlightened age, assisting and praising culture—refined elegance was called at its utmost flourishing.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor honored learning; his ministers, living in an age of enlightenment, assisted in spreading culture—a refinement acclaimed as reaching its zenith.

sentences.zh: 嘉慶以後，視學典禮，率循不廢。

translations.literal: After Jiaqing, the learning-inspection ceremony was generally followed without abandonment.
translations.idiomatic: After Jiaqing, the learning-inspection ceremony was generally maintained.

sentences.zh: 咸豐初，猶一舉行焉。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Xianfeng it was still held once.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Xianfeng it was still performed once.

sentences.zh: 道光末，詔整飭南學，住學者百餘人，監規頹廢已久，迄難振作。

translations.literal: At the end of Daoguang, an edict ordered rectification of the Southern Academy; more than a hundred resided for study, but directorate regulations had long decayed and were hard to revive.
translations.idiomatic: Late in Daoguang, an edict ordered reform of the Southern Academy. Though more than a hundred students resided there, Directorate regulations had long fallen into disuse and proved difficult to restore.

sentences.zh: 咸豐軍興，歲費折發，章程亦屢更。

translations.literal: When military campaigns began in Xianfeng, annual expenses were issued at reduced rates, and regulations were also repeatedly changed.
translations.idiomatic: With the outbreak of war in Xianfeng, annual allocations were cut and regulations repeatedly revised.

sentences.zh: 同治初元，以國學專課文藝，無裨實學，令兼課論、策。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Tongzhi, because the National University exclusively examined literary arts without benefit to practical learning, it was ordered also to examine disquisitions and policy essays.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Tongzhi, because the National University taught only literary arts without practical benefit, disquisitions and policy essays were added to the curriculum.

sentences.zh: 用經、史、性理諸書命題，獎勵留心時務者。

translations.literal: Topics were set from the classics, histories, and Nature and Principle texts, rewarding those attentive to current affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Examination topics drew on classics, histories, and Neo-Confucian texts, rewarding students attentive to current affairs.

sentences.zh: 明年，增發歲費三千兩。

translations.literal: The next year, three thousand additional taels of annual expense were disbursed.
translations.idiomatic: The following year, annual funding was increased by three thousand taels.

sentences.zh: 九年，乃復舊額。

translations.literal: In year 9, the old quota was restored.
translations.idiomatic: In Tongzhi 9, the original allocation was restored.

sentences.zh: 選文行優者四十人住南學，厚給廩餼，文風稍稍興起。

translations.literal: Forty persons of superior literary conduct were selected to reside at the Southern Academy, generously given stipends; literary style gradually revived.
translations.idiomatic: Forty students of superior scholarship were selected for the Southern Academy with generous stipends, and literary culture gradually revived.

sentences.zh: 光緒二年，增二十名。

translations.literal: In Guangxu 2, twenty places were added.
translations.idiomatic: In Guangxu 2 (1876), twenty additional places were created.

sentences.zh: 十一年，許各省舉人入監，曰舉監。

translations.literal: In year 11, provincial juren were permitted to enter the Directorate—called juren directorate students.
translations.idiomatic: In Guangxu 11 (1885), provincial juren were permitted to enter the Directorate as juren directorate students.

sentences.zh: 其後無論舉人、貢監生，凡非正印官未投供，舉、貢未傳到教習，均得入監，以廣裁成。

translations.literal: Thereafter whether juren or tribute and directorate students, all who were not principal appointees who had not presented service, or juren and tribute who had not yet been assigned teaching posts, were all permitted to enter the Directorate, to broaden cultivation.
translations.idiomatic: Thereafter juren and tribute or directorate students alike—whether or not they held principal appointments or teaching assignments—were permitted to enter the Directorate to broaden educational reach.

sentences.zh: 貢監生諸色目多沿明制，歲貢，取府、州、縣學食廩年深者，挨次升貢。

translations.literal: The various categories of tribute and directorate students mostly followed the Ming system. Annual tribute took those from prefectural, departmental, and district schools who had held stipends longest, advancing to tribute in order.
translations.idiomatic: Tribute and directorate student categories largely followed Ming practice. Annual tribute selected the longest-serving stipendiary students from prefectural, departmental, and district schools in order of seniority.

sentences.zh: 順治二年，命直省歲貢士京師。

translations.literal: In Shunzhi 2, it was ordered that provinces directly under the capital send annual tribute scholars to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: In Shunzhi 2 (1645), provinces were ordered to send annual tribute scholars to the capital.

sentences.zh: 府學歲一人，州學三歲二人，縣學二歲一人，一正二陪。

translations.literal: Prefectural schools one per year, departmental schools two every three years, district schools one every two years—one principal and two alternates.
translations.idiomatic: Prefectural schools sent one annually, departmental schools two every three years, district schools one every two years—one principal and two alternates each.

sentences.zh: 學政嚴加遴選，濫充發回原學。

translations.literal: Education intendants strictly selected; those unqualified were sent back to their original schools.
translations.idiomatic: Education intendants conducted strict selection; unqualified candidates were returned to their schools.

sentences.zh: 五名以上，學政罰俸。

translations.literal: Five or more such cases, and the education intendant was fined salary.
translations.idiomatic: Five or more such cases resulted in salary penalties for the education intendant.

sentences.zh: 十五年，令到部時詳查，年力強壯者，乃許送監。

translations.literal: In year 15, when they arrived at the ministry detailed inspection was ordered; only those vigorous in years and strength were permitted to be sent to the Directorate.
translations.idiomatic: In Shunzhi 15 (1658), candidates were inspected upon arrival at the ministry; only those still vigorous were sent to the Directorate.

sentences.zh: 康熙元年，減貢額，府三歲二人，州二歲一人，縣三歲一人。

translations.literal: In Kangxi 1, tribute quotas were reduced: prefectural schools two every three years, departmental one every two years, district one every three years.
translations.idiomatic: In Kangxi 1 (1662), tribute quotas were reduced to two per three years for prefectural schools, one per two years for departmental schools, and one per three years for district schools.

sentences.zh: 八年，復照順治二年例。

translations.literal: In year 8, the Shunzhi 2 precedent was restored.
translations.idiomatic: In Kangxi 8 (1669), the Shunzhi 2 quotas were restored.

sentences.zh: 二十六年，罷歲貢廷試。

translations.literal: In year 26, the annual tribute palace examination was abolished.
translations.idiomatic: In Kangxi 26 (1687), the palace examination for annual tribute students was abolished.

sentences.zh: 其後但由學政挨序考准咨部選授本省訓導。

translations.literal: Thereafter they were only examined in order by the education intendant, approved, referred to the ministry, and selected for appointment as instructors in their home province.
translations.idiomatic: Thereafter education intendants examined them in order, referred them to the ministry, and appointed them as provincial instructors.

sentences.zh: 得缺後，巡撫一加考驗，原入監者益鮮矣。

translations.literal: After receiving a post, the governor-general once more examined them; those originally entering the Directorate became ever rarer.
translations.idiomatic: After appointment, governors-general conducted an additional examination; fewer annual tribute students entered the Directorate.

sentences.zh: 恩貢，因明制，國家有慶典或登極詔書，以當貢者充之。

translations.literal: Grace tribute followed the Ming system: when the state had a celebration or an accession edict, the one due for tribute served.
translations.idiomatic: Grace tribute followed Ming practice: on state celebrations or imperial accessions, the student next in line for annual tribute was advanced as grace tribute.

sentences.zh: 順治元年，詔直省府、州、縣學，以本年正貢作恩貢，次貢作歲貢。

translations.literal: In Shunzhi 1, an edict ordered provincial prefectural, departmental, and district schools: that year's principal tribute became grace tribute, the next became annual tribute.
translations.idiomatic: In Shunzhi 1 (1644), an edict ordered that the year's principal tribute candidate become grace tribute and the next annual tribute.

sentences.zh: 歷代恩詔皆如之。

translations.literal: Grace edicts of successive generations all followed this.
translations.idiomatic: Subsequent grace edicts followed the same practice.

sentences.zh: 九年，五氏子孫觀禮生員十五人，送監讀書，准作恩貢。

translations.literal: In year 9, fifteen licentiates who were descendants of the Five Lineages observing the ceremony were sent to the Directorate to study, approved as grace tribute.
translations.idiomatic: In Shunzhi 9 (1652), fifteen licentiates from the Five Sage lineages who witnessed the ceremony were sent to the Directorate and granted grace tribute status.

sentences.zh: 乾隆後，恩賜臨雍觀禮聖賢后裔廩、增、附生入監以為常。

translations.literal: After Qianlong, grace grants to descendants of sages observing the ceremony at the emperor's presence at the Directorate, stipendiary, augmented, and attached students entering the Directorate, became regular.
translations.idiomatic: After Qianlong, it became regular practice to grant sage descendants who witnessed the imperial learning inspection entrance to the Directorate as stipendiary, augmented, or attached students.

sentences.zh: 至康、乾間，天子東巡，親詣闕里，拔取五氏、十三氏子孫生員貢成均，則加恩聖裔，非恆制也。

translations.literal: In the Kangxi and Qianlong period, when the Son of Heaven toured east, personally visited Qufu, and selected descendants of the Five and Thirteen Lineages as licentiates for tribute to the Imperial University—that was added grace to sage descendants, not the regular system.
translations.idiomatic: During the Kangxi and Qianlong reigns, when emperors toured the east and visited Qufu in person, selecting descendants of the Five and Thirteen Sage lineages for the Imperial University, this was special favor to sage descendants, not regular practice.

sentences.zh: 拔貢，因明選貢遺制，順治元年舉行。

translations.literal: Selected tribute followed the Ming selected-tribute legacy; it was instituted in Shunzhi 1.
translations.idiomatic: Selected tribute followed the Ming selected-tribute system, instituted in Shunzhi 1 (1644).

sentences.zh: 順天六人，直省府學二人，州、縣學各一人。

translations.literal: Shuntian six persons, provincial prefectural schools two, departmental and district schools one each.
translations.idiomatic: Shuntian sent six, each provincial prefectural school two, and each departmental and district school one.

sentences.zh: 康熙十年，令學臣於考取一、二等生員內，遴選文行兼優者貢太學，從祭酒查祿請也。

translations.literal: In Kangxi 10, education officials were ordered, among licentiates who passed first or second class, to select those combining literary and moral excellence for tribute to the Imperial University—following Libationer Cha Lu's request.
translations.idiomatic: In Kangxi 10 (1671), education officials were ordered to select first- and second-class licentiates of combined literary and moral excellence for the Imperial University, following Libationer Cha Lu's petition.

sentences.zh: 明年，始選拔八旗生員，滿洲、蒙古二人，漢軍一人。

translations.literal: The next year, Eight Banner licentiates were first selected: Manchu and Mongol two, Han Banner one.
translations.idiomatic: The following year, Eight Banner licentiates were first included: two Manchu and Mongol, one Han Banner.

sentences.zh: 時各省選貢多冒濫，三十七八年間，祭酒特默德、孫岳頒面試山西選拔張漢翀等六名，陝西呂爾恆等四名，廣東陳其瑋等三名，均文理不堪，字畫舛謬，原卷駁回，學臣參處，遂停選拔。

translations.literal: At this time selected tribute from all provinces was often fraudulent. In years 37–38, Libationers Temude and Sun Yueban personally examined six Shanxi selected candidates including Zhang Hanchong, four Shaanxi including Lü Erheng, three Guangdong including Chen Qiwei—all inadequate in literary principles, with erroneous characters; original papers were rejected, education officials were impeached, and selection was then stopped.
translations.idiomatic: Provincial selected tribute had become rife with unqualified candidates. In Kangxi 37–38, Libationers Temude and Sun Yueban personally examined Shanxi's six selected candidates including Zhang Hanchong, Shaanxi's four including Lü Erheng, and Guangdong's three including Chen Qiwei—all failed literary standards with erroneous characters. Their papers were rejected, education officials punished, and selection suspended.

sentences.zh: 雍正元年，禮部尚書陳元龍疏請嚴成均肄業之規。

translations.literal: In Yongzheng 1, Minister of Rites Chen Yuanlong memorialized requesting strict regulations for study at the Imperial University.
translations.idiomatic: In Yongzheng 1 (1723), Minister of Rites Chen Yuanlong petitioned for stricter Imperial University study regulations.

sentences.zh: 部議，太學監生，皆由捐納，能文之士稀少，應令學臣照舊例選拔送監。

translations.literal: The ministry deliberated: Imperial University directorate students all came through donation; able literary men were few; education officials should be ordered to select and send to the Directorate according to the old precedent.
translations.idiomatic: The ministry ruled that because directorate students entered through purchase and able scholars were scarce, education officials should resume selecting candidates for the Directorate.

sentences.zh: 從之。

translations.literal: Approval followed.
translations.idiomatic: The proposal was approved.

sentences.zh: 五年，世宗以歲貢較食廩淺深，多年力衰憊之人，欲得英才，必須選拔。

translations.literal: In year 5, the Shizong Emperor held that annual tribute compared stipend seniority shallow and deep, often producing persons feeble in years and strength; to obtain outstanding talent, selection was necessary.
translations.idiomatic: In Yongzheng 5 (1727), the Shizong Emperor observed that annual tribute based on stipend seniority often produced elderly candidates; to obtain outstanding talent, selection was essential.

sentences.zh: 命嗣後六年選拔一次。

translations.literal: It was ordered that hereafter selection occur once every six years.
translations.idiomatic: Selection was ordered every six years thereafter.

sentences.zh: 明年，又諭學政選拔不拘一、二等生員，酌試時務策論，果有識見才幹，再訪平日品行，即未列優等，亦許選拔。

translations.literal: The next year, education intendants were further instructed that selection was not confined to first- and second-class licentiates; they might try policy essays on current affairs, and if there were truly insight and ability, then inquire into daily conduct—even if not ranked superior, selection was still permitted.
translations.idiomatic: The following year, education intendants were instructed not to confine selection to first- and second-class licentiates but to test policy essays on current affairs; candidates demonstrating insight and ability, whatever their rank, could be selected after inquiry into their conduct.

sentences.zh: 故雍、乾間充貢國學，以選拔為最盛。

translations.literal: Thus in the Yongzheng and Qianlong period, filling tribute at the National University was most flourishing through selection.
translations.idiomatic: Selected tribute to the National University reached its peak under Yongzheng and Qianlong.

sentences.zh: 乾隆初定朝考制，列一、二等者，揀選引見錄用。

translations.literal: Early in Qianlong the court-examination system was fixed: those ranked first or second class were selected for audience and appointment.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Qianlong, the court examination system was established: first- and second-class candidates were selected for imperial audience and appointment.

sentences.zh: 三等劄監肄業。

translations.literal: Third class were ordered to pursue study at the Directorate.
translations.idiomatic: Third-class candidates were assigned to study at the Directorate.

sentences.zh: 尋停揀選例。

translations.literal: Soon the selection precedent was stopped.
translations.idiomatic: The selection procedure was soon discontinued.

sentences.zh: 三年期滿，祭酒等分別等第，覈實保薦，用知縣、教職。

translations.literal: When the three-year term was complete, libationer and others distinguished grades, verified and recommended, using them as magistrates and instructors.
translations.idiomatic: After three years, the libationer ranked students and recommended them for appointment as magistrates or instructors.

sentences.zh: 七年，帝以拔貢六年一舉，人多缺少，妨舉人銓選之路。

translations.literal: In year 7, the Emperor held that selected tribute every six years produced too many persons and shortages, obstructing juren selection routes.
translations.idiomatic: In Qianlong 7 (1742), the emperor held that selection every six years produced too many candidates and obstructed juren advancement.

sentences.zh: 且生員優者，應科舉時，自可脫穎而出，不專藉選拔為進身。

translations.literal: Moreover, superior licentiates at the civil examinations could naturally stand out; they need not rely solely on selection for advancement.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, outstanding licentiates could distinguish themselves at the civil examinations without relying solely on selection.

sentences.zh: 改十二年一舉。

translations.literal: It was changed to once every twelve years.
translations.idiomatic: The interval was changed to twelve years.

sentences.zh: 遂為永制。

translations.literal: This became the permanent system.
translations.idiomatic: This became permanent practice.

sentences.zh: 十六年，以天下教官多昏耄，濫竽戀棧。

translations.literal: In year 16, because instructors throughout the realm were mostly senile, many held posts unworthily and clung to their positions.
translations.idiomatic: In Qianlong 16 (1751), because instructors throughout the realm were often senile and unqualified yet clung to their posts,

sentences.zh: 雖定例六年甄別，長官每以閒曹，多方寬假。

translations.literal: although the fixed rule was triennial screening every six years, superiors often treated it as an idle post and granted wide indulgence.
translations.idiomatic: although regulations required review every six years, superiors often treated instructor posts as sinecures and granted excessive leniency.

sentences.zh: 諭詳加澄汰。

translations.literal: An edict ordered thorough clarification and elimination.
translations.idiomatic: An edict ordered thorough review and dismissal of unfit instructors.

sentences.zh: 廷臣議，督、撫三年澄汰教職員缺，以朝考揀選拔貢充補。

translations.literal: Court ministers deliberated: governors-general and governors every three years would clarify and eliminate instructor vacancies, using court-examination selection of selected tribute to fill them.
translations.idiomatic: Court ministers proposed that governors-general and governors review instructor vacancies every three years and fill them with selected tribute graduates from the court examination.

sentences.zh: 未入揀選者，劄監肄業如舊。

translations.literal: Those not entering selection received written orders to pursue study at the Directorate as before.
translations.idiomatic: Those not selected continued to study at the Directorate as before.

sentences.zh: 四十一年，定朝考優等兼用七品小京官。

translations.literal: In year 41, it was fixed that court-examination superior grades also used seventh-rank minor capital officials.
translations.idiomatic: In Qianlong 41 (1776), superior court examination graduates were also appointed seventh-rank capital officials.

sentences.zh: 五十五年，朝考始用覆試。

translations.literal: In year 55, the court examination first used re-examination.
translations.idiomatic: In Qianlong 55 (1790), re-examination was introduced for the court examination.

sentences.zh: 學政選拔分二場，試四書文、經文、策論。

translations.literal: Education intendant selection was divided into two sessions, testing Four Books essays, classic texts, and policy essays.
translations.idiomatic: Education intendant selection comprised two sessions testing Four Books essays, classic texts, and policy essays.

sentences.zh: 乾隆十七年，經文改經解。

translations.literal: In Qianlong 17, classic texts were changed to classic exegesis.
translations.idiomatic: In Qianlong 17 (1752), classic text examinations were changed to exegesis.

sentences.zh: 二十三年，增五言八韻詩。

translations.literal: In year 23, regulated verse in five characters and eight rhymes was added.
translations.idiomatic: In Qianlong 23 (1758), regulated verse in five characters and eight rhymes was added.

sentences.zh: 會同督、撫覆試。

translations.literal: Jointly with governors-general and governors, re-examination was held.
translations.idiomatic: Governors-general and governors conducted joint re-examinations.

sentences.zh: 朝考試書藝一、詩一。

translations.literal: The court examination tested one calligraphic composition and one poem.
translations.idiomatic: The court examination required one essay on calligraphy and one poem.

sentences.zh: 副榜入監，順治二年，令順天鄉試中式副榜增、附，准作貢監。

translations.literal: Supplementary-board entrants to the Directorate: in Shunzhi year 2, it was ordered that Shuntian provincial examination supplementary-board additional and supplementary licentiates be permitted to become tribute directorate students.
translations.idiomatic: Those who entered the Directorate via the supplementary board: in 1645, Shuntian provincial examinees on the supplementary list who were additional or supplementary licentiates were allowed to qualify as tribute students at the Directorate.

sentences.zh: 廩生及恩、拔、歲貢，免坐監，與廷試。

translations.literal: Grain-stipend licentiates and grace, selected, and annual tribute students were exempted from residence at the Directorate and joined the palace examination.
translations.idiomatic: Grain-stipend licentiates and grace, selected, and annual tribute students were exempt from studying at the Directorate and proceeded directly to the palace examination.

sentences.zh: 十五年，他貢停，惟副榜照舊解送。

translations.literal: In year 15, other tribute was stopped; only the supplementary board was sent up as before.
translations.idiomatic: In 1658, all other tribute categories were suspended; only supplementary-board candidates continued to be forwarded as before.

sentences.zh: 康熙元年，停副貢額。

translations.literal: In Kangxi year 1, the supplementary tribute quota was stopped.
translations.idiomatic: In 1662, the quota for supplementary tribute was abolished.

sentences.zh: 十一年，以查祿奏復，舊制優貢之選，與拔貢並重。

translations.literal: In year 11, on Zha Lu's memorial it was restored; the old system's selection of superior tribute was ranked equally with selected tribute.
translations.idiomatic: In 1672, on a memorial from Zha Lu, it was restored; under the former system, selection as superior tribute carried weight equal to selected tribute.

sentences.zh: 古順治二年，令直省不拘廩、增、附生，選文行兼優者，大學二人、小學一人送監。

translations.literal: Formerly in Shunzhi year 2, it was ordered that provinces not restrict grain-stipend, additional, or supplementary licentiates, but select those excellent in both letters and conduct—two from a large school, one from a small school—to be sent to the Directorate.
translations.idiomatic: As early as 1645, the court had ordered that provinces need not limit candidates to a single licentiate class, but choose men outstanding in scholarship and conduct—two from major prefectural schools and one from minor ones—for the Directorate.

sentences.zh: 康熙二十四年，以監生止輸納一途，貧窶之士無由觀光，令照順治二年例選送。

translations.literal: In Kangxi 24, because directorate students had only the route of payment, poor scholars had no means to come into the capital's light; it was ordered to select and send according to the Shunzhi year 2 precedent.
translations.idiomatic: In 1685, because admission to the Directorate had been reduced to purchase alone, impoverished scholars had no way to reach the capital; selection and forwarding were restored under the 1645 precedent.

sentences.zh: 雍正間，始析貢監名色，廩、增准作優貢，附生准作優監。

translations.literal: In the Yongzheng period, tribute-directorate designations were first distinguished: grain-stipend and additional licentiates might become superior tribute; supplementary licentiates might become superior directorate students.
translations.idiomatic: Under Yongzheng, tribute and directorate categories were first sorted out: grain-stipend and additional licentiates could qualify as superior tribute; supplementary licentiates as superior directorate students.

sentences.zh: 乾隆四年，限大省無過五、六名，中省三、四名，小省一、二名，任缺無濫。

translations.literal: In Qianlong 4, large provinces were limited to no more than five or six persons, medium provinces three or four, small provinces one or two, so vacancies were not filled indiscriminately.
translations.idiomatic: In 1739, large provinces were capped at five or six nominees, medium provinces at three or four, and small provinces at one or two, preventing indiscriminate filling of posts.

sentences.zh: 學政三年會同督、撫保題，分試兩場，略同選拔。

translations.literal: Every three years the education intendant, jointly with the governor-general and governor, submitted recommendations; examinations were divided into two sessions, broadly like selection tribute.
translations.idiomatic: Every three years the education intendant, acting with the governor-general and governor, submitted nominees for examination in two sessions, much like the selected-tribute procedure.

sentences.zh: 試四書文、經解、經文、策論，後增詩。

translations.literal: They tested Four Books essays, classic exegesis, classic texts, and policy essays; poetry was added later.
translations.idiomatic: Candidates sat for Four Books essays, exegesis, classic texts, and policy essays; poetry was added later.

sentences.zh: 二十三年，定優生到部，如拔貢朝考例。

translations.literal: In year 23, it was fixed that superior students arriving at the ministry should follow the court-examination precedent for selected tribute.
translations.idiomatic: In 1758, superior students reaching the ministry were placed under the same court-examination rules as selected tribute.

sentences.zh: 試書藝一、詩一，文理明通者升太學；

translations.literal: One calligraphic composition and one poem were tested; those clear and penetrating in letters and principles were promoted to the Imperial College;
translations.idiomatic: They were examined in one composition and one poem; those whose writing showed clarity and mastery were advanced to the Imperial College;

sentences.zh: 荒疏者發回，學政議處。

translations.literal: the crude and negligent were sent back, and the education intendant deliberated punishment.
translations.idiomatic: the crude or negligent were sent home for the education intendant to discipline.

sentences.zh: 二十九年，學臣有以拔貢年分暫停舉優為請者，部議拔貢十二年一舉，而學臣三年任滿，宜舉優黜劣，通省不過數名，應仍舊例。

translations.literal: In year 29, a provincial education commissioner requested temporarily suspending superior selection in selected-tribute years; the ministry deliberated that selected tribute was held every twelve years while commissioners served three-year terms, and that promoting the superior and demoting the inferior—no more than a few per province—should follow the old rule.
translations.idiomatic: In 1764, a provincial commissioner asked to suspend superior selection in years when selected tribute was held; the ministry ruled that with selected tribute every twelve years and commissioners serving three-year terms, each province should still nominate only a handful of superior candidates and demote the inferior, as before.

sentences.zh: 嘉慶十九年，御史黃中傑條奏，請與拔貢一體廷試錄用。

translations.literal: In Jiaqing 19, Censor Huang Zhongjie memorialized in separate articles, requesting that they join selected tribute in palace examination and appointment.
translations.idiomatic: In 1814, Censor Huang Zhongjie submitted a detailed memorial asking that superior students receive palace examination and appointment on the same terms as selected tribute.

sentences.zh: 禮部議駁。

translations.literal: The Ministry of Rites deliberated and rejected it.
translations.idiomatic: The Ministry of Rites deliberated and rejected the proposal.

sentences.zh: 請免來京朝考，示體恤。

translations.literal: He asked exemption from coming to the capital for the court examination, showing compassionate regard.
translations.idiomatic: He also asked that they be excused from traveling to the capital for the court examination, as a gesture of leniency.

sentences.zh: 帝以優生經朝考准作貢生，斯合貢於王廷之義。

translations.literal: The Emperor held that superior students, having passed the court examination and been approved as tribute students, fulfilled the meaning of presenting tribute at the royal court.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor replied that superior students who passed the court examination and were recognized as tribute students fulfilled the very meaning of presenting tribute at court.

sentences.zh: 停朝考，名實不符。

translations.literal: To stop the court examination would not match name and reality.
translations.idiomatic: Abolishing the court examination would make the title and the practice diverge.

sentences.zh: 弗許。

translations.literal: He did not permit it.
translations.idiomatic: He refused.

sentences.zh: 然卒以無錄用之條，多不赴京報考。

translations.literal: Yet in the end, because there was no provision for appointment, many did not go to the capital to sit the examination.
translations.idiomatic: In the end, however, with no path to office, many never traveled to the capital to take the examination.

sentences.zh: 同治二年，議定甲子科始廷試優生，仿順天鄉試例，分南、北、中卷。

translations.literal: In Tongzhi 2, it was deliberated and fixed that from the jiazi cycle palace examination of superior students would begin, following the Shuntian provincial examination precedent of southern, northern, and central examination rolls.
translations.idiomatic: In 1863, the court decided that beginning with the jiazi cycle, superior students would sit a palace examination divided, like the Shuntian provincial examination, into southern, northern, and central rolls.

sentences.zh: 八旗、奉天、直隸、山東、山西、河南、陝西、甘肅為北卷，江蘇、江西、浙江、安徽、福建、湖北、湖南為南卷，四川、廣東、廣西、雲南、貴州為中卷。

translations.literal: The Eight Banners, Fengtian, Zhili, Shandong, Shanxi, Henan, Shaanxi, and Gansu formed the northern roll; Jiangsu, Jiangxi, Zhejiang, Anhui, Fujian, Hubei, and Hunan the southern roll; Sichuan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Yunnan, and Guizhou the central roll.
translations.idiomatic: The northern roll comprised the Eight Banners, Fengtian, Zhili, Shandong, Shanxi, Henan, Shaanxi, and Gansu; the southern roll, Jiangsu, Jiangxi, Zhejiang, Anhui, Fujian, Hubei, and Hunan; the central roll, Sichuan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Yunnan, and Guizhou.

sentences.zh: 考列一、二等用知縣、教職，三等用訓導。

translations.literal: Those ranked first or second class were used as magistrates and instructors; third class as assistant instructors.
translations.idiomatic: First- and second-class graduates were appointed magistrates or instructors; third-class graduates, assistant instructors.

sentences.zh: 恩、拔、副、歲、優，時稱「五貢」。

translations.literal: Grace, selected, supplementary, annual, and superior tribute were at the time called the 'Five Tribute' categories.
translations.idiomatic: Grace, selected, supplementary, annual, and superior tribute were collectively known as the 'Five Tribute' categories.

sentences.zh: 科目之外，由此者謂之正途。

translations.literal: Outside the examination subjects, those advancing by these routes were called the regular path.
translations.idiomatic: Apart from the examination curriculum, advancement through these channels was termed the regular path.

sentences.zh: 所以別於雜流也。
