translations.literal: This was how they were distinguished from miscellaneous routes.
translations.idiomatic: Thus they were distinguished from irregular, purchased, or miscellaneous routes into office.

sentences.zh: 恩監，由八旗漢文官學生、算學滿、漢肄業生考取。

translations.literal: Grace directorate students were drawn from Eight Banners Chinese-language official school students and mathematics Manchu and Han students pursuing study.
translations.idiomatic: Grace directorate students came from graduates of the Eight Banners Chinese official schools and from Manchu and Han students completing the mathematics course.

sentences.zh: 又臨雍觀禮聖賢后裔，由武生、奉祀生、俊秀入監者，皆為恩監。

translations.literal: Also, at the imperial lecture-hall ceremonies, descendants of sages and worthies, military licentiates, ritual-attendant students, and distinguished youths entering the Directorate were all grace directorate students.
translations.idiomatic: So were descendants of sages who attended imperial lecture ceremonies, military licentiates, ritual-attendant students, and distinguished youths admitted to the Directorate—all counted as grace directorate students.

sentences.zh: 例貢與例監相仿，由廩、增、附生或俊秀監生援例報捐貢生者，曰例貢；

translations.literal: Precedent tribute resembled precedent directorate students: grain-stipend, additional, or supplementary licentiates, or distinguished directorate students who reported donation for tribute student status, were called precedent tribute;
translations.idiomatic: Precedent tribute paralleled precedent directorate status: grain-stipend, additional, or supplementary licentiates, or distinguished directorate students who purchased tribute standing, were termed precedent tribute;

sentences.zh: 由俊秀報捐監生者，曰例監。

translations.literal: distinguished youths who reported donation for directorate student status were called precedent directorate students.
translations.idiomatic: distinguished youths who purchased directorate standing were termed precedent directorate students.

sentences.zh: 凡捐納入官必由之。

translations.literal: All who entered office by donation had to pass through this.
translations.idiomatic: Every route into office through purchase had to pass through these categories.

sentences.zh: 或在監肄業，或在籍，均為監生。

translations.literal: Whether pursuing study in the Directorate or remaining on the registers at home, all were directorate students.
translations.idiomatic: Whether studying at the Directorate or remaining on local registers, all were counted as directorate students.

sentences.zh: 恩廕，凡滿、漢子弟奉敕送監讀書，恩詔分別內外文武品級，廕子入監。

translations.literal: Grace yin privilege: whenever Manchu and Han sons were sent by imperial order to study at the Directorate, grace edicts distinguished civil and military ranks inside and outside the capital, and yin sons entered the Directorate.
translations.idiomatic: Grace yin privilege: when Manchu and Han officials' sons were sent by imperial order to the Directorate, successive grace edicts set civil and military rank thresholds at court and in the provinces, and yin sons were admitted.

sentences.zh: 順治二年，定文官京四品、外三品以上，武官二品以上，俱送一子入監。

translations.literal: In Shunzhi 2, it was fixed that civil officials of the fourth rank and above in the capital and third rank and above in the provinces, and military officials of the second rank and above, all sent one son to the Directorate.
translations.idiomatic: In 1645, civil officials of fourth rank or higher at court and third rank or higher in the provinces, and military officials of second rank or higher, were each required to send one son to the Directorate.

sentences.zh: 十一年，覺羅廕生照各官廕生例，一體送監。

translations.literal: In year 11, Aisin Gioro yin students followed the precedent for officials' yin students and were sent to the Directorate alike.
translations.idiomatic: In 1654, Aisin Gioro yin students were placed on the same footing as other officials' yin sons and sent to the Directorate.

sentences.zh: 包衣佐領下官子弟，向例不得為廕監。

translations.literal: Sons of officials under banner company commanders who were bond servants had by precedent not been permitted yin directorate status.
translations.idiomatic: Sons of bond-servant officials under company commanders had traditionally been barred from yin admission to the Directorate.

sentences.zh: 康熙九年，例除。

translations.literal: In Kangxi 9, the precedent was removed.
translations.idiomatic: In 1670, that restriction was lifted.

sentences.zh: 宗室給廕入監，自康熙五十二年始也。

translations.literal: Imperial clansmen receiving yin admission to the Directorate began in Kangxi 52.
translations.idiomatic: Yin admission for imperial clansmen began in 1713.

sentences.zh: 難廕始順治四年，以殉難陝西固原道副使呂鳴夏子入監讀書。

translations.literal: Martyrdom yin began in Shunzhi 4, when the son of Lü Mingxia, vice commissioner of the Shaanxi Guyuan circuit who died for the dynasty, was admitted to study at the Directorate.
translations.idiomatic: Martyrdom yin dated from 1647, when the son of Lü Mingxia—vice commissioner on the Shaanxi Guyuan circuit, who died in service—was admitted to the Directorate.

sentences.zh: 九年，定內、外滿、漢三品以上官，三年任滿，勤事以死者，廕一子入監。

translations.literal: In year 9, it was fixed that inner and outer Manchu and Han officials of the third rank and above, upon completing a three-year term and dying in diligent service, might yin one son into the Directorate.
translations.idiomatic: In 1652, officials of third rank or higher—Manchu and Han, at court or in the provinces—who completed a three-year term and died in diligent service could yin one son into the Directorate.

sentences.zh: 後廣其例，凡三司首領，州、縣佐貳官死難者，亦得廕子矣。

translations.literal: Later the precedent was broadened: heads of the three provincial commissions and assistant prefectural and county officials who died in martyrdom might also yin a son.
translations.idiomatic: Later the rule was widened so that heads of provincial commissions and assistant prefectural and county officials who died in martyrdom could yin a son as well.

sentences.zh: 外國肄業生，康熙二十七年，琉球國王始遣陪臣子弟梁成楫等隨貢使至，入貢肄業。

translations.literal: Foreign students pursuing study: in Kangxi 27, the king of Ryukyu first sent attendant ministers' sons Liang Chengji and others with the tribute mission; they entered tribute study.
translations.idiomatic: Foreign students at the Directorate: in 1688, the king of Ryukyu first sent the sons of attendant ministers, including Liang Chengji, with the tribute embassy to pursue study there.

sentences.zh: 雍正六年，鄂羅斯遣官生魯喀等留學中國，以滿、漢助教等教之，月給銀米器物，學成遣歸，先後絡繹。

translations.literal: In Yongzheng 6, Russia sent official students such as Luka to remain and study in China; Manchu and Han assistant instructors taught them, with monthly supplies of silver, grain, and goods; when study was complete they were sent home—such missions came in succession.
translations.idiomatic: In 1728, Russia sent students such as Luka to remain in China; Manchu and Han assistant instructors taught them on a monthly stipend of silver, grain, and supplies, and when their studies ended they were sent home—missions of this kind followed one after another.

sentences.zh: 至同治間，琉球官生猶有至者。

translations.literal: Down to the Tongzhi period, Ryukyuan official students still arrived.
translations.idiomatic: As late as the Tongzhi era, Ryukyuan students were still arriving.

sentences.zh: 他如順治二年，於隨征入關奉天十五學，取三十人入監，為天下勸。

translations.literal: Other cases: in Shunzhi 2, from the fifteen Fengtian schools that had followed the campaign south, thirty persons were taken into the Directorate to encourage the realm.
translations.idiomatic: Among other cases, in 1645 thirty students were chosen from the fifteen Fengtian schools that had followed the Qing armies through the pass and admitted to the Directorate as a model for the empire.

sentences.zh: 十一年，定隨征廩生准作貢監。

translations.literal: In year 11, it was fixed that grain-stipend licentiates who had followed the campaign might become tribute directorate students.
translations.idiomatic: In 1654, campaign-following grain-stipend licentiates were permitted to become tribute directorate students.

sentences.zh: 生員有軍功二等，准作生監。

translations.literal: Licentiates with second-class military merit were permitted to become student directorate status.
translations.idiomatic: Licentiates with second-class military merit could qualify as student directorate status.

sentences.zh: 更有軍功二等，准作貢生，謂之功貢。

translations.literal: With further second-class military merit, they were permitted to become tribute students—called merit tribute.
translations.idiomatic: With a further second-class merit citation, they could qualify as tribute students—termed merit tribute.

sentences.zh: 未幾例停，則開國時權宜之制也。

translations.literal: Before long the precedent was stopped; it was an expedient of the founding period.
translations.idiomatic: The practice was soon discontinued—a wartime expedient of the dynasty's founding years.

sentences.zh: 考送校錄，始於乾隆三年，令國子監選正途貢生，年力少壯、字畫端楷者十人，送武英殿備謄錄。

translations.literal: Examination and forwarding for collation copyists began in Qianlong 3, when the Directorate was ordered to choose ten regular-path tribute students, young in years and upright in handwriting, to be sent to the Hall of Military Glory as collation copyists.
translations.idiomatic: Selection of collation copyists began in 1738, when the Directorate was told to nominate ten young regular-path tribute students with neat script for copying duty at the Hall of Military Glory.

sentences.zh: 年滿議敘。

translations.literal: When the term was complete, merits were deliberated for reward.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of their term, merits were reviewed for promotion.

sentences.zh: 三十四年例停，歸吏部謄錄貢生內選取。

translations.literal: In year 34 the precedent was stopped; selection reverted to collation tribute students within the Ministry of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: In 1769 the Directorate route was closed; selection returned to collation tribute students under the Ministry of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 嗣以吏部無合例者，仍由在監拔、副、優貢生考選。

translations.literal: Later, because the ministry had no qualified candidates, selection again came from selected, supplementary, and superior tribute students at the Directorate.
translations.idiomatic: When the ministry later lacked qualified men, selection again fell to selected, supplementary, and superior tribute students in the Directorate.

sentences.zh: 嘉慶間增十名，後不復行。

translations.literal: In the Jiaqing period ten additional posts were added; the practice was not resumed afterward.
translations.idiomatic: During Jiaqing ten additional posts were authorized, but the expansion was not continued.

sentences.zh: 五貢就職，學政會同巡撫驗看，咨部依科分名次、年分先後，恩、拔、副貢以教諭選用，歲貢以訓導選用。

translations.literal: When the Five Tribute took office, the education intendant jointly with the provincial governor inspected them and reported to the ministry; according to examination cycle ranking and year order, grace, selected, and supplementary tribute were chosen as instructors, annual tribute as assistant instructors.
translations.idiomatic: When Five Tribute graduates took up posts, the education intendant and governor inspected them and reported to the ministry; by examination cycle and seniority, grace, selected, and supplementary tribute were appointed instructors, annual tribute assistant instructors.

sentences.zh: 康熙中，捐納歲貢，並用訓導。

translations.literal: In the Kangxi period, purchased annual tribute also used assistant instructors.
translations.idiomatic: Under Kangxi, purchased annual tribute was likewise appointed to assistant instructorships.

sentences.zh: 雍正初，捐納貢生，教諭改縣丞，訓導改主簿。

translations.literal: Early in Yongzheng, purchased tribute students had instructors changed to assistant magistrates and assistant instructors to chief clerks.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Yongzheng, purchased tribute students who would have become instructors were made assistant magistrates instead, and assistant instructors chief clerks.

sentences.zh: 既仍許廩生捐歲貢者，用訓導；

translations.literal: Thereafter grain-stipend licentiates who purchased annual tribute still used assistant instructors;
translations.idiomatic: Thereafter grain-stipend licentiates who purchased annual tribute still took assistant instructorships;

sentences.zh: 恩、拔、副貢年力富強者，得就職直隸州州判。

translations.literal: grace, selected, and supplementary tribute who were robust in years might take office as assistant judges of direct-administration prefectures.
translations.idiomatic: while robust grace, selected, and supplementary tribute graduates could take posts as assistant judges in Zhili prefectures.

sentences.zh: 嘉慶以後，凡朝考未錄之拔貢及恩、副、歲、優貢生，遇鄉試年，得具呈就職、就教。

translations.literal: After Jiaqing, all selected tribute not appointed at the court examination and all grace, supplementary, annual, and superior tribute students, in provincial examination years, might submit petitions to take office or take instructorships.
translations.idiomatic: After Jiaqing, selected tribute not placed at the court examination and all grace, supplementary, annual, and superior tribute students could, in provincial examination years, petition to take civil posts or teaching appointments.

sentences.zh: 優貢就教，附歲貢末用訓導。

translations.literal: Superior tribute taking instructorships was appended after annual tribute and used assistant instructorships.
translations.idiomatic: Superior tribute seeking instructorships were ranked after annual tribute and assigned assistant instructorships.

sentences.zh: 道光初，許滿、蒙正途貢生就職，與滿員通較年分先後選用。

translations.literal: Early in Daoguang, Manchu and Mongol regular-path tribute students were permitted to take office, compared for seniority with Manchu posts.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Daoguang, Manchu and Mongol regular-path tribute students were allowed to take office, their seniority weighed together with Manchu appointees.

sentences.zh: 貢監考職，定例必監期已滿，乃許送考。

translations.literal: For tribute and directorate examination for office, the fixed rule required that the Directorate term be complete before forwarding for examination was permitted.
translations.idiomatic: For the tribute-directorate examination for office, regulations required completion of the Directorate term before a candidate could be forwarded.

sentences.zh: 惟特恩考職，不論監期滿否。

translations.literal: Only for special-grace examination for office was completion of the Directorate term disregarded.
translations.idiomatic: Only in special-grace examination years was the Directorate term requirement waived.

sentences.zh: 凡正途、捐納各項貢、監生，及候補訁謄錄、教習、校錄，一體送考。

translations.literal: All regular-path and purchased tribute and directorate students, and candidates awaiting collation copyist, instructor, and proofreader posts, were sent to examination alike.
translations.idiomatic: All regular-path and purchased tribute and directorate students, together with candidates awaiting collation, instructorship, or proofreader posts, sat the examination alike.

sentences.zh: 其已就教、就職及捐職、襲世職者不許。

translations.literal: Those who had already taken instructorships or office, or purchased office, or inherited hereditary posts were not permitted.
translations.idiomatic: Those already in teaching posts or office, who had purchased rank, or who held inherited posts were ineligible.

sentences.zh: 初制，考職歲一舉，貢、監一例以州同、州判、縣丞、主簿、吏目錄用。

translations.literal: Under the initial system, examination for office was held annually; tribute and directorate students alike were recorded for assistant prefect, assistant judge, assistant magistrate, chief clerk, and clerical posts.
translations.idiomatic: Originally the examination for office was annual; tribute and directorate students alike were registered for assistant prefect, assistant judge, assistant magistrate, chief clerk, and clerical posts.

sentences.zh: 乾隆元年，定考職以鄉試年，恩科不考。

translations.literal: In Qianlong 1, it was fixed that examination for office followed provincial examination years; grace-cycle examinations did not hold it.
translations.idiomatic: In 1736, the examination for office was tied to provincial examination years and was not held in grace-cycle years.

sentences.zh: 恩、拔、副貢考列一等以州同、二等以州判、三等以縣丞選用。

translations.literal: Grace, selected, and supplementary tribute ranked first class were chosen as assistant prefects, second class as assistant judges, third class as assistant magistrates.
translations.idiomatic: Grace, selected, and supplementary tribute who ranked first class were appointed assistant prefects, second class assistant judges, third class assistant magistrates.

sentences.zh: 歲貢一等以主簿、二等以吏目選用。

translations.literal: Annual tribute first class were chosen as chief clerks, second class as clerical posts.
translations.idiomatic: Annual tribute of first class became chief clerks; second class, clerical posts.

sentences.zh: 原就教者聽。

translations.literal: Those who originally sought instructorships were left to their choice.
translations.idiomatic: Candidates who had originally sought instructorships were left free to keep them.

sentences.zh: 捐納貢監考取如歲貢例。

translations.literal: Purchased tribute and directorate students who passed followed the annual tribute precedent.
translations.idiomatic: Purchased tribute and directorate students who passed were appointed under the annual tribute rules.

sentences.zh: 五十六年停考職。

translations.literal: In year 56 examination for office was stopped.
translations.idiomatic: In 1791 the examination for office was suspended.

sentences.zh: 嘉慶五年，僅一行之。

translations.literal: In Jiaqing 5 it was held only once.
translations.idiomatic: In 1800 it was held only once more.

sentences.zh: 光緒三十一年，直隸總督袁世凱等奏停科舉摺寬籌舉貢生員出路一條，「請十年三科內優貢加額錄取。

translations.literal: In Guangxu 31, Governor-General Yuan Shikai of Zhili and others memorialized on widening outlets for tribute students and licentiates when the examinations were stopped, 'requesting increased quotas for superior tribute selection within three cycles over ten years.
translations.idiomatic: In 1905, Yuan Shikai, governor-general of Zhili, and others memorialized on creating outlets for tribute students and licentiates after the abolition of the civil examinations, proposing 'expanded quotas for superior tribute within three examination cycles over ten years.

sentences.zh: 己酉選拔如舊，朝考用京官知縣。

translations.literal: The jiyou cycle selection tribute as before; court examination to use capital officials and magistrates.
translations.idiomatic: Selected tribute in the jiyou cycle to continue as before; court examination graduates to receive capital posts or magistracies.

sentences.zh: 督、撫、學政三科內考選學貢通算學、地理、財政、兵事、交涉、鐵路、礦務、警察、外國政法之一者，三年一次，保送若干名，略視會試中額兩三倍。

translations.literal: Within three cycles governors-general, governors, and education intendants were to examine and choose academic tribute proficient in one of mathematics, geography, finance, military affairs, foreign relations, railways, mining, police, or foreign law; once every three years a certain number were to be forwarded—roughly two or three times the metropolitan examination quota.
translations.idiomatic: Over three cycles, governors and education intendants would examine and forward academic tribute skilled in mathematics, geography, finance, military affairs, diplomacy, railways, mining, police work, or foreign law; every three years a cohort roughly two or three times the metropolitan quota would be sent to the capital.

sentences.zh: 赴京試取者，用主事、中書、知縣」。

translations.literal: Those who passed examination in the capital were used as secretaries, Hanlin compilers, and magistrates.'
translations.idiomatic: Those who passed in the capital would be appointed secretaries, Hanlin compilers, or magistrates.'

sentences.zh: 詔議行。

translations.literal: An edict ordered deliberation and implementation.
translations.idiomatic: The throne ordered the proposals deliberated and carried out.

sentences.zh: 明年，政務處詳議，己酉拔貢，照向額倍取，本年丙午考優。

translations.literal: The next year the Office of Government Affairs deliberated in detail: jiyou selected tribute would take double the usual quota; in the current bingwu year superior tribute would be examined.
translations.idiomatic: The following year the Office of Government Affairs worked out the details: jiyou selected tribute would double its quota; superior tribute would be examined in the current bingwu year.

sentences.zh: 以後三年一考，視例額加四倍。

translations.literal: Thereafter examination would be every three years, with four times the usual quota.
translations.idiomatic: Thereafter examinations would be held every three years at four times the standing quota.

sentences.zh: 廩生出貢許倍額。

translations.literal: Grain-stipend licentiates advancing to tribute were permitted double quotas.
translations.idiomatic: Grain-stipend licentiates nominated for tribute might be doubled in number.

sentences.zh: 部院考用謄錄，分舉人、五貢、生員三等。

translations.literal: Ministries and courts examined and employed collation copyists, divided into three grades: juren, Five Tribute, and licentiates.
translations.idiomatic: Ministries and courts examined collation copyists in three grades: juren, Five Tribute graduates, and licentiates.

sentences.zh: 二年期滿獎敘。

translations.literal: After a two-year term, rewards of rank were granted.
translations.idiomatic: After two years, meritorious service was rewarded with promotion.

sentences.zh: 舉人、優、拔，擇尤改用七品小京官。

translations.literal: Juren and superior and selected tribute, the most outstanding were changed to seventh-rank minor capital officials.
translations.idiomatic: The best juren and superior or selected tribute graduates could be promoted to seventh-rank minor capital posts.

sentences.zh: 又為廣就職之例，五貢一體以直隸州州判，按察、鹽運經歷，散州州判、經歷，縣丞，分別註選，或分發試用。

translations.literal: The precedent for taking office was also broadened: all Five Tribute alike might be registered for assistant judges of Zhili prefectures, provincial surveillance and salt transport secretaries, assistant judges and secretaries of independent prefectures, and assistant magistrates, with separate notation for selection or probationary dispatch.
translations.idiomatic: Rules for taking office were widened as well: all Five Tribute graduates could be registered for Zhili assistant judges, provincial surveillance and salt-transport secretaries, prefectural assistant judges and secretaries, and assistant magistracies, either for formal selection or probationary assignment.

sentences.zh: 蓋五貢終清之世，未嘗廢棄也。

translations.literal: Thus the Five Tribute were never abandoned throughout the Qing.
translations.idiomatic: In this way the Five Tribute categories endured through the entire Qing dynasty.

sentences.zh: 算學隸國子監，稱國子監算學。

translations.literal: Mathematics was subordinate to the Directorate of Education and was called the Directorate Mathematics School.
translations.idiomatic: Mathematics was administered under the Directorate of Education as the Directorate Mathematics School.

sentences.zh: 乾隆四年，額設學生滿、漢各十二，蒙古、漢軍各六。

translations.literal: In Qianlong 4, quotas were set at twelve Manchu and twelve Han students, six Mongol and six Han Banner students.
translations.idiomatic: In 1739 quotas were set at twelve Manchu and twelve Han students, plus six Mongol and six Han Banner students.

sentences.zh: 續設漢肄業生二十四。

translations.literal: Han students pursuing study were later added, twenty-four in number.
translations.idiomatic: Twenty-four additional Han students pursuing study were later enrolled.

sentences.zh: 遵御制數理精蘊，分線、面、體三部。

translations.literal: Following the imperially endorsed Principles of Mathematical Astronomy, the curriculum was divided into three parts: lines, surfaces, and solids.
translations.idiomatic: Following the emperor's Principles of Mathematical Astronomy, instruction was divided into three parts: lines, surfaces, and solids.

sentences.zh: 部限一年通曉。

translations.literal: Each part was limited to one year for mastery.
translations.idiomatic: Each part had to be mastered within one year.

sentences.zh: 七政限二年。

translations.literal: The seven luminaries were limited to two years.
translations.idiomatic: The seven luminaries required two years.

sentences.zh: 有季考、歲考。

translations.literal: There were quarterly and annual examinations.
translations.idiomatic: Quarterly and annual examinations were held.

sentences.zh: 五年期滿考取者，滿、蒙、漢軍學生咨部，以本旗天文生序補。

translations.literal: Those who passed examination at the end of the five-year term—Manchu, Mongol, and Han Banner students—were reported to the ministry and filled astronomical posts in their banners in order.
translations.idiomatic: After five years, Manchu, Mongol, and Han Banner students who passed were reported to the ministry and appointed astronomical officers in their banners by seniority.

sentences.zh: 漢學生舉人用博士，貢監生童用天文生。

translations.literal: Han students: juren were used as erudites; tribute, directorate, and licentiate students as astronomical officers.
translations.idiomatic: Han students who were juren became erudites; tribute students, directorate students, and licentiates became astronomical officers.

sentences.zh: 此外隸國學者，為八旗官學。

translations.literal: Besides these, those subordinate to the Imperial College were the Eight Banners official schools.
translations.idiomatic: Beyond these, schools under the Imperial College included the Eight Banners official schools.

sentences.zh: 順治元年，若琳奏：「臣監僻在城東北隅，滿員子弟就學不便，議於滿洲八固山地方各立書院，以國學二廳、六堂教官分教之，以時赴監考課。」

translations.literal: In Shunzhi 1, Ruolin memorialized: "The Directorate lies remote in the northeastern corner of the city; it is inconvenient for Banner members' sons to attend school. It is proposed to establish academies in each of the Manchu Eight Banner garrison areas, with the Imperial College's two halls and six hall instructors dividing instruction, and to come to the Directorate at intervals for examinations."
translations.idiomatic: In 1644, Director Ruolin memorialized: "The Imperial College stands in an out-of-the-way corner northeast of the city, making attendance difficult for Banner youths. We propose establishing academies in each Manchu Banner garrison, with instructors from the College's two halls and six lecture halls teaching locally and reporting to the Directorate for periodic examinations."

sentences.zh: 下部議行。

translations.literal: The memorial was forwarded to the ministries for deliberation and implementation.
translations.idiomatic: The ministries deliberated and approved.

sentences.zh: 於是八旗各建學舍。

translations.literal: Thereupon each of the Eight Banners built school quarters.
translations.idiomatic: Each Banner thereupon built school quarters.

sentences.zh: 每佐領下取官學生一名，以十名習漢書，餘習滿書。

translations.literal: Under each company commander one official school student was taken; of every ten, they studied Chinese books, the rest Manchu books.
translations.idiomatic: Each company commander nominated one official school student; one in ten studied Chinese texts, the remainder Manchu script.

sentences.zh: 二年，從所蘊言，合兩旗為一學。

translations.literal: In year 2, following Suoyun's proposal, two banners were combined into one school.
translations.idiomatic: In 1645, on Suoyun's recommendation, two Banners were merged into a single school.

sentences.zh: 每學教習十人，教習酌取京省生員。

translations.literal: Each school had ten instructors; instructors were drawn as appropriate from capital and provincial licentiates.
translations.idiomatic: Each school employed ten instructors, chosen as appropriate from licentiates in the capital and provinces.

sentences.zh: 其後學額屢有增減，教習於國學肄業生考選，止用恩、拔、副、歲貢生。

translations.literal: Later enrollment was repeatedly increased or reduced; instructors were selected from students pursuing study at the Imperial College, using only grace, selected, supplementary, and annual tribute students.
translations.idiomatic: Enrollment quotas were later adjusted repeatedly; instructors were chosen from students at the Imperial College, limited to grace, selected, supplementary, and annual tribute graduates.

sentences.zh: 如無其人，準例監生亦得考取。

translations.literal: If none were available, precedent directorate students might also be admitted by examination.
translations.idiomatic: When no such candidates existed, precedent directorate students could also qualify by examination.

sentences.zh: 舉人原就，一例考選。

translations.literal: Presented licentiates originally serving might also be selected by examination on the same terms.
translations.idiomatic: Serving presented licentiates were likewise eligible for selection by examination on the same terms.

sentences.zh: 雍正元年，於八旗蒙古護軍、領催、驍騎內，選熟練國語、蒙古語者十六人，充蒙古教習。

translations.literal: In Yongzheng 1, from among Banner Mongol guards, squad leaders, and vanguard cavalry, sixteen skilled in Manchu and Mongol were chosen as Mongol instructors.
translations.idiomatic: In 1723, sixteen Banner Mongols from the guards, squad leaders, and vanguard cavalry who were proficient in Manchu and Mongol were appointed Mongol-language instructors.

sentences.zh: 向例官學生分佐領選送。

translations.literal: By former precedent official school students were selected and sent by company commander.
translations.idiomatic: Under former rules, official school students were nominated and sent by company commander.

sentences.zh: 五年，定每旗額設百名。

translations.literal: In year 5, each banner's quota was fixed at one hundred.
translations.idiomatic: In 1727, each Banner's enrollment was fixed at one hundred.

sentences.zh: 滿洲六十，習清、漢書各半。

translations.literal: For Manchu, sixty—half studied Manchu books, half Chinese books.
translations.idiomatic: Sixty places were for Manchus, half studying Manchu texts and half Chinese.

sentences.zh: 蒙古、漢軍各二十，通一旗選擇，不拘佐領。

translations.literal: Mongol and Han Banner, twenty each; selection was banner-wide without restriction to company.
translations.idiomatic: Mongol and Han Banners had twenty each; selection was banner-wide and not confined to individual companies.

sentences.zh: 年幼者習清書，稍長者習漢文。

translations.literal: Younger ones studied Manchu books; older ones Chinese literature.
translations.idiomatic: Younger students studied Manchu script; older ones Chinese literature.

sentences.zh: 撥八旗教養兵額滿洲三十，蒙古、漢軍各十名錢糧分給學生。

translations.literal: Thirty Manchu, ten Mongol, and ten Han Banner educational stipend soldier quotas were allocated; grain pay was distributed to students.
translations.idiomatic: Thirty Manchu, ten Mongol, and ten Han Banner educational stipend soldier quotas were assigned, and their grain pay distributed to students.

sentences.zh: 定漢教習每旗五人。

translations.literal: Chinese instructors were fixed at five per banner.
translations.idiomatic: Five Chinese instructors were fixed per Banner.

sentences.zh: 乾隆初，定官學生肄業以十年為率，三年內講誦經書，監臣考驗，擇材資聰穎有志力學者，歸漢文班；

translations.literal: Early Qianlong: official school students' course of study was set at ten years as standard; within the first three years they lectured on the classics and the Directorate minister examined them; those of keen talent and ambition for study were assigned to the Chinese class;
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Qianlong reign, the standard course for official school students was set at ten years; in the first three years they studied the classics under examination by the Directorate minister, and those of keen talent and scholarly ambition were placed in the Chinese class;

sentences.zh: 年長原學繙譯者，歸滿文班。

translations.literal: those older who had originally studied translation were assigned to the Manchu class.
translations.idiomatic: older students who had originally pursued translation were placed in the Manchu class.

sentences.zh: 三年，欽派大臣考取漢文明通者，拔為監生，升太學。

translations.literal: In year 3, an imperially dispatched minister examined those proficient in Chinese and selected them as directorate students for promotion to the Imperial University.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year, an imperially appointed minister examined those proficient in Chinese and advanced them as directorate students to the Imperial University.

sentences.zh: 與漢貢監究心明經治事，期滿，擇尤保薦，考選錄用。

translations.literal: With Han tribute and directorate students they devoted themselves to mastering the classics and practical affairs; when the term was complete, the outstanding were recommended for examination and selection for appointment.
translations.idiomatic: Together with Han tribute and directorate students they pursued the classics and practical governance; at term's end the outstanding were recommended for examination and appointment.

sentences.zh: 八年，定漢教習三年期滿，分等引見。

translations.literal: In year 8, Chinese instructors' three-year term was fixed; upon completion they were presented by rank.
translations.idiomatic: In 1743, the three-year term for Chinese instructors was fixed; upon completion they were presented to the throne by grade.

sentences.zh: 一等用知縣，二等用知縣或教職銓選。

translations.literal: First class appointed magistrate; second class magistrate or educational office by selection.
translations.idiomatic: First-class graduates were appointed magistrates; second-class, magistrates or educational posts by selection.

sentences.zh: 一等再教習三年，果實心訓課者，知縣即用。

translations.literal: First class who served another three years as instructor and truly instructed diligently could be appointed magistrate immediately.
translations.idiomatic: First-class instructors who served another three years and truly taught with dedication could be appointed magistrate outright.

sentences.zh: 蒙古教習五年期滿實心訓課者，用護軍校、驍騎校。

translations.literal: Mongol instructors after five years' term and diligent instruction were appointed guard sergeants or vanguard sergeants.
translations.idiomatic: Mongol instructors who completed five years and taught diligently were appointed guard or vanguard sergeants.

sentences.zh: 滿助教每旗二人，以八旗文進士、舉人，繙譯進士、舉人，恩、拔、副、歲貢生，文生員，繙譯生員，廢員，筆帖式考取。

translations.literal: Manchu assistant instructors, two per banner, were chosen from Eight Banners civil jinshi and licentiates, translation jinshi and licentiates, grace, selected, supplementary, and annual tribute students, civil licentiates, translation licentiates, dismissed officials, and clerks.
translations.idiomatic: Two Manchu assistant instructors per Banner were chosen from Eight Banners civil jinshi and licentiates, translation jinshi and licentiates, grace, selected, supplementary, and annual tribute students, civil and translation licentiates, dismissed officials, and clerks.

sentences.zh: 三十三年，下五旗包衣每旗增設學生十名。

translations.literal: In year 33, for the five lower banners' bondservants, ten additional students per banner.
translations.idiomatic: In 1768, for bondservants of the five lower Banners, ten additional students per Banner were authorized.

sentences.zh: 滿洲六，蒙古、漢軍各二，不給錢糧。

translations.literal: Manchu six, Mongol and Han Banner two each; no grain pay given.
translations.idiomatic: Six Manchu, two Mongol, and two Han Banner places—without grain stipends.

sentences.zh: 五十四年，於每旗百名內裁十名，選取經書熟、文理優者二十人，加給膏火資鼓勵。

translations.literal: In year 54, within each banner's hundred places ten were cut; twenty with mature classics and superior literary skill received additional stipends as encouragement.
translations.idiomatic: In 1789, ten places were cut from each Banner's quota of one hundred; twenty students with thorough command of the classics and superior literary skill received additional stipends as encouragement.

sentences.zh: 嘉、道以後，官學積漸廢弛，八旗子弟僅恃此進身。

translations.literal: After Jiaqing and Daoguang, official schools gradually declined; Banner sons relied on this alone for advancement.
translations.idiomatic: After the Jiaqing and Daoguang reigns, official schools gradually decayed, and Banner youths depended on them alone for advancement.

sentences.zh: 教習停年期滿予錄用例，月課虛應故事。

translations.literal: Instructors on leave at term's end received appointment by precedent; monthly examinations were empty formality.
translations.idiomatic: Instructors received routine appointment when their terms ended; monthly examinations became hollow formalities.

sentences.zh: 雖明諭屢督責，迄難振刷。

translations.literal: Though clear edicts repeatedly urged and supervised, revival remained difficult.
translations.idiomatic: Though repeated imperial edicts urged reform, revitalization proved impossible.

sentences.zh: 光緒初，力籌整頓。

translations.literal: Early Guangxu, vigorous efforts were made to reorganize.
translations.idiomatic: In the early Guangxu period, serious efforts were made to reorganize the schools.

sentences.zh: 每學以滿、漢科甲官一人為管學官，專司考覈學生課程，教習勤惰。

translations.literal: Each school had one Manchu or Han jinshi official as school superintendent to examine students' curriculum and instructors' diligence.
translations.idiomatic: Each school was assigned one Manchu or Han jinshi official as superintendent to oversee students' coursework and instructors' diligence.

sentences.zh: 簡派滿、漢進士出身大員二人為管理八旗官學大臣。

translations.literal: Two high officials of jinshi rank, Manchu and Han, were appointed to manage Eight Banners official schools.
translations.idiomatic: Two senior officials of jinshi rank, one Manchu and one Han, were appointed commissioners for the Eight Banners official schools.

sentences.zh: 每學添設翰林編、檢一員。

translations.literal: Each school added one Hanlin compiler or reviewer.
translations.idiomatic: Each school added one Hanlin compiler or reviewer.

sentences.zh: 月課季考，分司考校。

translations.literal: Monthly and seasonal examinations—divided responsibility for examination.
translations.idiomatic: Monthly and seasonal examinations were assigned to different officers for supervision.

sentences.zh: 春秋赴監會考如舊。

translations.literal: Spring and autumn they went to the Directorate for joint examination as before.
translations.idiomatic: In spring and autumn they still reported to the Directorate for joint examinations as before.

sentences.zh: 同、光間，國學及官學造就科舉之才，亦頗稱盛。

translations.literal: During Tongzhi and Guangxu, the Imperial College and official schools produced examination talent in considerable abundance.
translations.idiomatic: During the Tongzhi and Guangxu reigns, the Imperial College and official schools still produced a considerable number of examination graduates.

sentences.zh: 然囿於帖括，舊制鮮變通。

translations.literal: Yet confined to the eight-legged essay, old institutions scarcely adapted.
translations.idiomatic: Yet instruction remained confined to the eight-legged essay, and the old institutions scarcely changed.

sentences.zh: 三十一年，監臣奏於南學添設科學，未幾，裁國子監，並設學部。

translations.literal: In year 31 the Directorate minister memorialized adding sciences at the Southern Academy; soon the Imperial Directorate was abolished and the Ministry of Education established.
translations.idiomatic: In 1905 the Directorate minister memorialized adding modern sciences at the Southern Academy; soon the Imperial Directorate was abolished and the Ministry of Education established.

sentences.zh: 文廟祀典，設國子丞一人掌之。

translations.literal: Confucian temple sacrificial rites were managed by one Guozi assistant director.
translations.idiomatic: Sacrificial rites at the Confucian temple were placed under one assistant director of the former Directorate.

sentences.zh: 八旗官學改並學堂，算學亦改稱欽天監天文算學，隸欽天監。

translations.literal: Eight Banners official schools were merged into schools; mathematics study was renamed Astronomical and Mathematical Study under the Astronomical Directorate.
translations.idiomatic: Eight Banners official schools were merged into modern schools; the mathematics course was renamed the Astronomical and Mathematical Study and placed under the Astronomical Directorate.

sentences.zh: 而太學遂與科舉並廢雲。

translations.literal: Thus the Imperial University and examinations were abolished together.
translations.idiomatic: Thus the Imperial University and the examination system were abolished together.

sentences.zh: 宗學肇自虞廷，命夔典樂，教胄子。

translations.literal: Imperial clan schools originated in the court of Yu; Kui was ordered to preside over music and teach the heir's sons.
translations.idiomatic: Imperial clan schools originated in the court of Yu, when Kui was ordered to preside over music and instruct the heir's sons.

sentences.zh: 三代無宗學名，而義已備。

translations.literal: The Three Dynasties had no name "imperial clan school," yet the meaning was complete.
translations.idiomatic: The Three Dynasties had no term "imperial clan school," yet the institution was fully in place.

sentences.zh: 唐、宋後，有其名而制弗詳。

translations.literal: After Tang and Song the name existed but the institution was not detailed.
translations.idiomatic: After Tang and Song the name existed, but the regulations were not set out in detail.

sentences.zh: 清順治十年，八旗各設宗學，選滿洲生員為師。

translations.literal: In Qing Shunzhi 10 each banner established an imperial clan school, choosing Manchu licentiates as teachers.
translations.idiomatic: In Shunzhi 10 of the Qing, each Banner established an imperial clan school and chose Manchu licentiates as teachers.

sentences.zh: 凡未封宗室子弟，十歲以上，俱入學習清書。

translations.literal: All unenfeoffed imperial clansmen's sons ten years and above all entered to study Manchu books.
translations.idiomatic: All sons of unenfeoffed clansmen aged ten or above entered to study Manchu script.

sentences.zh: 雍正二年定制，左、右兩翼設滿、漢學各一，王、公、將軍及閒散宗室子弟十八歲以下，入學分習清、漢書，兼騎射。

translations.literal: Yongzheng 2 regulations: left and right wings each had Manchu and Chinese schools; princes, dukes, generals, and idle clansmen under eighteen entered to study Manchu or Chinese and archery.
translations.idiomatic: In Yongzheng 2 regulations were fixed: the left and right wings each had Manchu and Chinese schools; princes, dukes, generals, and idle clansmen under eighteen entered to study Manchu or Chinese and archery.

sentences.zh: 以王、公一人總其事。

translations.literal: One prince or duke supervised overall.
translations.idiomatic: One prince or duke supervised the whole.

sentences.zh: 設總、副管，以宗室分尊齒長者充之。

translations.literal: Chief and deputy superintendents were filled by clansmen of seniority and age.
translations.idiomatic: Chief and deputy superintendents were filled by clansmen of senior rank and age.

sentences.zh: 清書教習二人，選罷閒旗員及進士、舉人、貢生、生員善繙譯者充之。

translations.literal: Two Manchu book instructors—chosen from idle banner members and jinshi, licentiates, tribute students, and licentiates skilled at translation.
translations.idiomatic: Two Manchu-script instructors were chosen from idle Banner members and from jinshi, licentiates, tribute students, and licentiates skilled in translation.

sentences.zh: 騎射教習二人，選罷閒旗員及護軍校善射者充之。

translations.literal: Two archery instructors—idle banner members and guard sergeants skilled at shooting.
translations.idiomatic: Two archery instructors were chosen from idle Banner members and guard sergeants skilled in archery.

sentences.zh: 每學生十人，設漢書教習一人，禮部考取舉、貢充之。

translations.literal: Per ten students one Chinese instructor—Ministry of Rites examined and appointed licentiates or tribute students.
translations.idiomatic: For every ten students one Chinese instructor was appointed, examined and assigned by the Ministry of Rites from licentiates or tribute students.

sentences.zh: 三年期滿，分別等第錄用。

translations.literal: Three-year term complete—ranked by grade and appointed.
translations.idiomatic: Upon completing a three-year term, instructors were ranked by grade and appointed.

sentences.zh: 十一年，兩學各以翰林官二人董率課程，分日講授經義、文法。

translations.literal: Year 11: each school had two Hanlin officials to direct curriculum, lecturing classics and grammar on alternate days.
translations.idiomatic: In year 11, each school had two Hanlin officials to direct the curriculum, lecturing on the classics and grammar on alternate days.

sentences.zh: 乾隆初，以滿、漢京堂各一人總稽學課，月試經義、繙譯及射藝。

translations.literal: Early Qianlong: one Manchu and one Han capital official each supervised; monthly tests on classics, translation, and archery.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Qianlong, one Manchu and one Han capital official each supervised instruction; monthly examinations covered classics, translation, and archery.

sentences.zh: 九年，定每屆五年，簡大臣合試兩翼學生，欽定名次，以會試中式註冊。

translations.literal: Year 9: every five years a minister was dispatched for joint examination of both wings' students; ranks imperially fixed; registered as passed metropolitan examination.
translations.idiomatic: In year 9, every five years a minister was dispatched to examine students of both wings jointly; ranks were fixed by imperial order and they were registered as having passed the metropolitan examination.

sentences.zh: 俟會試年，習繙譯者，與八旗繙譯貢生同引見，賜進士，用府屬額外主事。

translations.literal: When metropolitan examination year came, translation students together with Eight Banners translation tribute students were presented, granted jinshi, appointed extra secretaries in prefectural administrations.
translations.idiomatic: In metropolitan examination years, students of translation, together with Eight Banners translation tribute students, were presented, granted jinshi, and appointed extra secretaries in prefectural administrations.

sentences.zh: 習漢文者，與天下貢士同殿試，賜進士甲第，用翰林部屬等官。

translations.literal: Chinese students took palace examination with all tribute scholars, granted jinshi ranks, appointed Hanlin and ministry posts etc.
translations.idiomatic: Students of Chinese took the palace examination with all tribute scholars, were granted jinshi ranks, and appointed to Hanlin and ministry posts.

sentences.zh: 十年，考試漢文、繙譯無佳作。

translations.literal: Year 10: examination of Chinese and translation produced no fine compositions.
translations.idiomatic: In year 10, examinations in Chinese and translation produced no fine compositions.

sentences.zh: 諭曰：「我朝崇尚本務，宗室子弟俱講究清文，精通騎射。

translations.literal: Edict: "Our dynasty esteems fundamental duties; imperial clansmen all study Manchu and master archery.
translations.idiomatic: An edict stated: "Our dynasty esteems fundamental duties; imperial clansmen should all study Manchu and master archery.

sentences.zh: 誠恐學習漢文，流於漢人浮靡之習。

translations.literal: Truly fearing study of Chinese would lead to Han frivolous habits.
translations.idiomatic: We truly fear that studying Chinese will lead them into the frivolous habits of the Han.

sentences.zh: 世祖諭停習漢書，所以敦本實、黜浮華也。

translations.literal: Shizu ordered cessation of Chinese study to consolidate substance and reject ornament.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Shizu ordered the cessation of Chinese study in order to strengthen substance and reject ornament.

sentences.zh: 嗣後宗室子弟不能習漢文者，其各嫺習武藝，儲為國家有用之器。」

translations.literal: Hereafter clansmen unable to study Chinese should each be skilled in martial arts, stored as useful instruments for the state."
translations.idiomatic: Hereafter, clansmen unable to study Chinese should each be skilled in martial arts and prepared as useful servants of the state."

sentences.zh: 明年，定學額，左翼七十，右翼六十。

translations.literal: Next year quotas fixed: left wing 70, right wing 60.
translations.idiomatic: The next year quotas were fixed: seventy for the left wing, sixty for the right.

sentences.zh: 二十一年，裁漢教習九人，改繙譯教習。

translations.literal: Year 21: cut nine Chinese instructors, changed to translation instructors.
translations.idiomatic: In year 21, nine Chinese instructors were cut and replaced with translation instructors.

sentences.zh: 增騎射教習，翼各一人。

translations.literal: Increased archery instructors, one per wing.
translations.idiomatic: Archery instructors were increased to one per wing.

sentences.zh: 嘉慶初，畫一兩翼學額，增右翼十名。

translations.literal: Early Jiaqing: unified both wings' quotas, added ten to right wing.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Jiaqing, the quotas of both wings were unified and ten places added to the right wing.

sentences.zh: 定每學教習滿三人，漢四人。

translations.literal: Fixed each school three Manchu instructors, four Chinese.
translations.idiomatic: Each school was fixed at three Manchu instructors and four Chinese.

sentences.zh: 十三年，兩翼各增學額三十，足百名，為永制。

translations.literal: Year 13: each wing added thirty places, full hundred—permanent institution.
translations.idiomatic: In year 13, each wing added thirty places, bringing the total to one hundred—a permanent quota.

sentences.zh: 覺羅學，雍正七年，詔八旗於衙署旁設滿、漢學各一，覺羅子弟八歲至十八歲，入學讀書習射，規制略同宗學。

translations.literal: Aisin Gioro schools—Yongzheng 7: ordered Eight Banners to establish Manchu and Chinese schools beside yamen; Aisin Gioro sons eight to eighteen entered to read and shoot; regulations roughly like clan schools.
translations.idiomatic: Aisin Gioro schools: in Yongzheng 7, the Eight Banners were ordered to establish Manchu and Chinese schools beside their yamen; Aisin Gioro sons aged eight to eighteen entered to read and practice archery, on regulations roughly like imperial clan schools.

sentences.zh: 總管王、公，春秋考驗。

translations.literal: Supervised by prince or duke; spring and autumn examination.
translations.idiomatic: A prince or duke served as superintendent; examinations were held in spring and autumn.

sentences.zh: 三年欽派大臣會同宗人府考試，分別獎懲。

translations.literal: Every three years imperial minister jointly with Imperial Clan Court examined; rewards and punishments by rank.
translations.idiomatic: Every three years an imperially appointed minister examined jointly with the Imperial Clan Court, with rewards and punishments by rank.

sentences.zh: 學成，與旗人同應歲、科試及鄉、會試，並考用中書、筆帖式。

translations.literal: Upon completion of study, with Banner people they took annual and triennial exams and provincial and metropolitan exams; also examined for secretary and clerk posts.
translations.idiomatic: Upon completing their studies, they took the same annual, triennial, provincial, and metropolitan examinations as other Banner people and were examined for secretary and clerk posts.

sentences.zh: 學額鑲黃旗六十一，正黃旗三十六，正白旗、正紅旗各四十，鑲白旗十五，鑲紅旗六十四，正藍旗三十九，鑲藍旗四十五。

translations.literal: Quotas: Bordered Yellow 61, Plain Yellow 36, Plain White and Plain Red 40 each, Bordered White 15, Bordered Red 64, Plain Blue 39, Bordered Blue 45.
translations.idiomatic: Enrollment quotas were: Bordered Yellow 61, Plain Yellow 36, Plain White and Plain Red 40 each, Bordered White 15, Bordered Red 64, Plain Blue 39, Bordered Blue 45.

sentences.zh: 滿、漢教習，旗各二人。

translations.literal: Manchu and Han instructors, two each per banner.
translations.idiomatic: Manchu and Han instructors, two each per Banner.

sentences.zh: 惟鑲白旗各一。

translations.literal: Only Bordered White Banner one each.
translations.idiomatic: Only the Bordered White Banner had one each.

sentences.zh: 景山官學，康熙二十四年，令於北上門兩旁官房設官學，選內府三旗佐領、管領下幼童三百六十名。

translations.literal: Jingshan official school—Kangxi 24: north of Meridian Gate official houses set as school; 360 young boys from inner three banners' company commanders and stewards selected.
translations.idiomatic: Jingshan official school: in Kangxi 24, official quarters north of the Meridian Gate were set up as a school, and 360 young boys were chosen from company commanders and stewards of the inner three banners.

sentences.zh: 清書三房，各設教習三人。

translations.literal: Manchu script: three rooms, three instructors each.
translations.idiomatic: For Manchu script, three rooms were set up, each with three instructors.

sentences.zh: 漢書三房，各設教習四人。

translations.literal: Chinese books: three rooms, four instructors each.
translations.idiomatic: For Chinese books, three rooms were set up, each with four instructors.

sentences.zh: 初，滿教習用內府官老成者，漢教習禮部考取生員文理優通者。

translations.literal: At first Manchu instructors were veteran inner-palace officials; Chinese instructors were licentiates of superior literary skill examined by the Ministry of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: At first Manchu instructors were seasoned inner-palace officials; Chinese instructors were licentiates of superior literary skill examined by the Ministry of Rites.

sentences.zh: 尋改選內閣善書、射之中書充滿教習，新進士老成者充漢教習。

translations.literal: Soon changed to secretaries of the Grand Secretariat skilled in calligraphy and archery for Manchu instructors, and seasoned new jinshi for Chinese instructors.
translations.idiomatic: Soon the selection changed to Grand Secretariat secretaries skilled in calligraphy and archery for Manchu instructors, and seasoned new jinshi for Chinese instructors.

sentences.zh: 雍正後，漢教習以舉人、貢生考取，三年期滿，咨部敘用。

translations.literal: After Yongzheng, Chinese instructors were chosen from licentiates and tribute students; upon three-year completion, the Ministry was consulted for appointment.
translations.idiomatic: After Yongzheng, Chinese instructors were chosen from licentiates and tribute students; upon completing three years, the Ministry of Personnel was consulted for appointment.

sentences.zh: 學生肄業三年，考列一等用筆帖式，二等用庫使、庫守。

translations.literal: Students pursuing three years' study: first class appointed clerk; second class warehouse attendant or keeper.
translations.idiomatic: After three years of study, first-class students were appointed clerks; second-class, warehouse attendants or keepers.

sentences.zh: 乾隆四十四年，許回子佐領下選補學生四名。

translations.literal: Qianlong 44: four students from Muslim company commanders permitted.
translations.idiomatic: In Qianlong 44, four students from Muslim company commanders were permitted to enroll.

sentences.zh: 嘉慶間，定額鑲黃旗、正白旗均百二十四，正黃旗百四十，回童四。

translations.literal: Jiaqing period quotas: Bordered Yellow and Plain White 124 each, Plain Yellow 140, Muslim youths 4.
translations.idiomatic: During Jiaqing, quotas were fixed at Bordered Yellow and Plain White 124 each, Plain Yellow 140, and four Muslim youths.

sentences.zh: 咸安宮官學，雍正六年，詔選內府三旗佐領、管領下幼童及八旗俊秀者九十名，以翰林官居住咸安宮教之。

translations.literal: Xian'an Palace official school—Yongzheng 6: ninety young boys from inner three banners and outstanding Banner youths chosen; Hanlin officials resided at Xian'an Palace to teach them.
translations.idiomatic: Xian'an Palace official school: in Yongzheng 6, ninety young boys from the inner three banners and outstanding Banner youths were chosen, and Hanlin officials residing at Xian'an Palace were appointed to teach them.

sentences.zh: 漢書十二房，清書三房，各設教習一人，教射、教國語，各三人，如景山官學考取例。

translations.literal: Twelve Chinese rooms, three Manchu rooms, one instructor each; archery and Manchu language, three each—as at Jingshan official school examination precedent.
translations.idiomatic: Twelve Chinese rooms and three Manchu rooms each had one instructor; archery and Manchu language had three each, on the same selection rules as Jingshan official school.

sentences.zh: 五年欽派大臣考試，一、二等用七、八品筆帖式。

translations.literal: Every five years an imperial minister examined; first and second class appointed seventh- and eighth-rank clerks.
translations.idiomatic: Every five years an imperial minister examined them; first- and second-class graduates were appointed seventh- and eighth-rank clerks.

sentences.zh: 漢教習三年、清語騎射教習五年，分別議敘。

translations.literal: Chinese instructors three years, Manchu-language and archery instructors five years—merits deliberated separately.
translations.idiomatic: Chinese instructors served three years, Manchu-language and archery instructors five years—merits were deliberated separately for appointment.

sentences.zh: 乾隆初，定漢教習選取新進士，不足，於明通榜舉人考充。

translations.literal: Early Qianlong: Chinese instructors chosen from new jinshi; if insufficient, presented licentiates from the Mingtong list were examined and appointed.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Qianlong, Chinese instructors were chosen from new jinshi; if insufficient, presented licentiates from the Mingtong list were examined and appointed.

sentences.zh: 期滿，進士用主事、知縣，舉人用知縣、教職。

translations.literal: Upon completion, jinshi appointed secretary or magistrate; licentiates magistrate or educational posts.
translations.idiomatic: Upon completion, jinshi were appointed secretaries or magistrates; licentiates, magistrates or educational posts.

sentences.zh: 二十三年以後，不論年分，許學生考繙譯中書、筆帖式、庫使。

translations.literal: After year 23, regardless of years of study, students might be examined for translation secretary, clerk, or warehouse attendant.
translations.idiomatic: 23 years later, regardless of years enrolled, students might be examined for translation secretary, clerk, or warehouse attendant.

sentences.zh: 定教習漢九人，滿六人。

translations.literal: Fixed nine Chinese instructors, six Manchu.
translations.idiomatic: Quotas were fixed at nine Chinese instructors and six Manchu.

sentences.zh: 宗學、覺羅學隸宗人府，景山學、咸安宮學隸內務府。

translations.literal: Imperial clan and Aisin Gioro schools were under the Imperial Clan Court; Jingshan and Xian'an Palace schools under the Imperial Household Department.
translations.idiomatic: Imperial clan and Aisin Gioro schools were under the Imperial Clan Court; Jingshan and Xian'an Palace schools under the Imperial Household Department.

sentences.zh: 諸學總管、教習等，類乏通才，經費徒糜。

translations.literal: Superintendents and instructors alike lacked able talent; funds were wasted in vain.
translations.idiomatic: Superintendents and instructors alike generally lacked able talent, and funds were wasted to no purpose.

sentences.zh: 甚者黌舍空虛，期滿時，例報成就學生若干名而已。

translations.literal: In extreme cases schoolhouses stood empty; at term's end they merely reported by precedent a certain number of students having completed study.
translations.idiomatic: In the worst cases schoolhouses stood empty; at term's end they merely reported by precedent that a certain number of students had completed their studies.

sentences.zh: 光緒二十八年，翰林院侍讀寶熙奏請援同文館歸併大學堂例，將宗室、覺羅、八旗等官學改並中、小學堂，均歸管學大臣辦理。

translations.literal: Guangxu 28: Hanlin reader-in-waiting Bao Xi memorialized requesting, following the precedent of merging the Tongwen Guan into the university, that imperial clan, Aisin Gioro, and Eight Banners official schools be merged into primary and secondary schools, all under the commissioner of education.
translations.idiomatic: In 1902, Hanlin reader-in-waiting Bao Xi memorialized that, following the precedent of merging the Tongwen Guan into the university, imperial clan, Aisin Gioro, and Eight Banners official schools should be merged into primary and secondary schools, all under the commissioner of education.

sentences.zh: 從之。

translations.literal: Approved.
translations.idiomatic: The court approved.

sentences.zh: 他如世職官學，八旗及禮部義學，健銳營、外火器營、圓明園、護軍營等學，皆清代特設，習滿、蒙語言文字。

translations.literal: Others such as hereditary-office official schools, Eight Banners and Ministry of Rites charity schools, the Vanguard Camp, Outer Firearms Camp, Yuanmingyuan, and Guard schools—all were specially established in the Qing and taught Manchu and Mongol language and script.
translations.idiomatic: Other institutions included hereditary-office official schools, Eight Banners and Ministry of Rites charity schools, and schools of the Vanguard Camp, Outer Firearms Camp, Yuanmingyuan, and Guard Corps—all Qing foundations for Manchu and Mongol language and script.

sentences.zh: 府、州、縣、衛儒學，明制具備，清因之。

translations.literal: Confucian schools at prefectures, departments, counties, and guards: the Ming system was complete, and the Qing followed it.
translations.idiomatic: Confucian schools at the prefectural, departmental, county, and guard levels followed the fully developed Ming system.

sentences.zh: 世祖勘定天下，命賑助貧生，優免在學生員，官給廩餼。

translations.literal: When the Founding Emperor pacified the realm, he ordered relief for poor students, exemptions for students in school, and official grain stipends.
translations.idiomatic: When the Shunzhi Emperor pacified the realm, he ordered relief for impoverished students, privileges for enrolled licentiates, and official grain stipends.

sentences.zh: 順治七年，改南京國子監為江寧府學。

translations.literal: In Shunzhi 7, the Nanjing Imperial Directorate was changed to Jiangning prefectural school.
translations.idiomatic: In 1650, the Nanjing Imperial Directorate was converted into the Jiangning prefectural school.

sentences.zh: 尋頒臥碑文，刊石立直省學宮。

translations.literal: Soon the reclining-stele inscription was promulgated, carved on stone and erected at provincial school temples.
translations.idiomatic: Soon the reclining-stele inscription was issued, carved in stone, and set up at provincial Confucian schools.

sentences.zh: 諭禮部曰：「帝王敷治，文教為先。

translations.literal: An edict to the Ministry of Rites stated: "When emperors spread governance, literary instruction comes first.
translations.idiomatic: An edict to the Ministry of Rites read: "When emperors govern, cultural instruction comes first.

sentences.zh: 臣子致君，經術為本。

translations.literal: When ministers serve their ruler, classical learning is the foundation.
translations.idiomatic: When ministers serve their sovereign, classical learning is the foundation.

sentences.zh: 自明末擾亂，日尋干戈，學問之道，闕焉未講。

translations.literal: Since the disturbances of late Ming, days were spent in warfare, and the way of learning was left untaught.
translations.idiomatic: Since the turmoil of late Ming, warfare consumed each day, and scholarly instruction was neglected.

sentences.zh: 今天下漸定，朕將興文教，崇經術，以開太平。

translations.literal: Now that the realm is gradually settled, I shall promote literary instruction, honor classical learning, and open the way to great peace.
translations.idiomatic: Now that the realm is gradually settled, I shall promote literary instruction, honor the classics, and open the age of great peace.

sentences.zh: 爾部傳諭直省學臣，訓督士子，凡理學、道德、經濟、典故諸書，務研求淹貫。

translations.literal: Your ministry shall transmit orders to provincial education commissioners to instruct and supervise scholars; all books on Neo-Confucian principle, morality, statecraft, and historical precedent must be thoroughly mastered.
translations.idiomatic: Your ministry shall instruct provincial education commissioners to train scholars in Neo-Confucian principle, moral conduct, statecraft, and historical precedent until they are thoroughly mastered.

sentences.zh: 明體則為真儒，達用則為良吏。

translations.literal: Those who clarify substance become true Confucians; those who reach application become good officials.
translations.idiomatic: Those who grasp principle become true scholars; those who apply it become capable officials.

sentences.zh: 果有實學，朕必不次簡拔，重加任用。」

translations.literal: If there is genuine learning, I shall certainly promote out of turn and employ with high honor."
translations.idiomatic: Those who show genuine learning I shall promote without regard to seniority and employ with distinction."

sentences.zh: 初，各省設督學道，以各部郎中進士出身者充之。

translations.literal: At first each province established an education circuit, filled by department directors of jinshi origin.
translations.idiomatic: At first each province had an education circuit, staffed by ministry directors who were jinshi graduates.

sentences.zh: 惟順天、江南、浙江為提督學政，用翰林官。

translations.literal: Only Shuntian, Jiangnan, and Zhejiang had education commissioners as superintendents, using Hanlin officials.
translations.idiomatic: Only Shuntian, Jiangnan, and Zhejiang had superintending education commissioners drawn from the Hanlin.

sentences.zh: 宣大、蘇松、江安、淮揚、肇高先皆分設，既乃裁併。

translations.literal: Xuanda, Sujiang, Jiangan, Huaiyang, and Zhaoqing were first separately established, then later merged.
translations.idiomatic: Circuits for Xuanda, Sujiang, Jiangan, Huaiyang, and Zhaoqing were first set up separately and later merged.

sentences.zh: 上下江、湖南北則裁併後仍分設。

translations.literal: Upper and Lower Yangzi and Hunan-Hubei were split again after merger.
translations.idiomatic: The Upper and Lower Yangzi and Hunan-Hubei circuits were re-divided after an earlier merger.

sentences.zh: 雍正中，一體改稱學院，省設一人。

translations.literal: In the Yongzheng period all were uniformly renamed education commissioners, one per province.
translations.idiomatic: In the Yongzheng period all were uniformly renamed education commissioners, with one per province.

sentences.zh: 奉天以府丞、台灣以台灣道兼之。

translations.literal: Fengtian was combined with the prefectural vice commissioner; Taiwan with the Taiwan circuit intendant.
translations.idiomatic: Fengtian was assigned to the prefectural vice commissioner; Taiwan to the Taiwan circuit intendant.

sentences.zh: 甘肅自分闈後，始設學政。

translations.literal: Gansu, after separate examination halls were established, first received an education commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: Gansu received an education commissioner only after its own examination hall was established.

sentences.zh: 各學教官，府設教授，州設學正，縣設教諭，各一，皆設訓導佐之。

translations.literal: Instructors at each school: prefectures had one professor, departments one director of studies, counties one instructor—each with an assistant instructor.
translations.idiomatic: Each school had instructors: prefectures a professor, departments a director of studies, counties an instructor—each assisted by an assistant instructor.

sentences.zh: 員額時有裁併。

translations.literal: Establishment quotas were periodically cut or merged.
translations.idiomatic: Staff quotas were periodically reduced or merged.

sentences.zh: 生員色目，曰廩膳生、增廣生、附生。

translations.literal: Categories of licentiates were grain-stipend students, additional students, and supplementary students.
translations.idiomatic: Licentiates were classified as grain-stipend, additional, and supplementary students.

sentences.zh: 初入學曰附學生員。

translations.literal: Those first entering school were called supplementary licentiates.
translations.idiomatic: New entrants were called supplementary licentiates.

sentences.zh: 廩、增有定額，以歲、科兩試等第高者補充。

translations.literal: Grain-stipend and additional places had fixed quotas, filled by highest ranks in annual and triennial examinations.
translations.idiomatic: Grain-stipend and additional quotas were fixed and filled by top ranks in the annual and triennial school examinations.

sentences.zh: 生員額初視人文多寡，分大、中、小學。

translations.literal: Licentiate quotas at first depended on local culture, divided into large, medium, and small schools.
translations.idiomatic: Licentiate quotas at first varied with local scholarly culture, divided among large, medium, and small schools.

sentences.zh: 大學四十名，中學三十名，小學二十名。

translations.literal: Large schools forty places, medium thirty, small twenty.
translations.idiomatic: Large schools had forty places, medium thirty, and small twenty.

sentences.zh: 嗣改府視大學，大州、縣視中學減半，小學四名或五名。

translations.literal: Later prefectures were treated as large schools, large departments and counties as medium schools halved, small schools four or five places.
translations.idiomatic: Later prefectures were treated as large schools; large departments and counties as medium schools at half quota; small schools four or five places.

sentences.zh: 康熙九年，大府、州、縣仍舊額，更定中學十二名，小學七名或八名。

translations.literal: In Kangxi 9 large prefectures, departments, and counties kept old quotas; medium schools were fixed at twelve, small at seven or eight.
translations.idiomatic: In 1670 large prefectures, departments, and counties kept their old quotas; medium schools were fixed at twelve places and small at seven or eight.

sentences.zh: 後屢有增廣。

translations.literal: Later there were repeated increases.
translations.idiomatic: Quotas were later increased repeatedly.

sentences.zh: 滿洲、蒙古、漢軍子弟，初歸順天考試取進，滿洲、漢軍各百二十名，蒙古六十名。

translations.literal: Manchu, Mongol, and Han Banner sons at first took entrance examinations through Shuntian; Manchu and Han Banner 120 each, Mongol 60.
translations.idiomatic: Manchu, Mongol, and Han Banner youths at first entered through Shuntian examinations: 120 each for Manchu and Han Banner, 60 for Mongol.

sentences.zh: 康熙中減定滿、蒙四十名，漢軍二十名。

translations.literal: In the Kangxi period this was reduced to Manchu and Mongol 40, Han Banner 20.
translations.idiomatic: Under Kangxi this was reduced to 40 for Manchu and Mongol and 20 for Han Banner.

sentences.zh: 旋復增為滿、蒙六十，漢軍三十。

translations.literal: Soon it was increased again to Manchu and Mongol 60, Han Banner 30.
translations.idiomatic: It was soon raised again to 60 for Manchu and Mongol and 30 for Han Banner.

sentences.zh: 學政三年任滿。

translations.literal: Education commissioners served three-year terms.
translations.idiomatic: Education commissioners served three-year terms.

sentences.zh: 歲、科兩試。

translations.literal: Annual and triennial examinations.
translations.idiomatic: They held annual and triennial examinations.

sentences.zh: 順治十五年停直省科試，康熙十二年復之。

translations.literal: In Shunzhi 15 triennial provincial examinations were suspended; in Kangxi 12 they were restored.
translations.idiomatic: Triennial provincial licentiate examinations were suspended in 1658 and restored in 1673.

sentences.zh: 儒童入學考試，初用四書文、孝經論各一，孝經題少，又以性理、太極圖說、通書、西銘、正蒙命題。

translations.literal: Entrance examinations for schoolboys at first used one Four Books essay and one Classic of Filial Piety discourse; because Filial Piety topics were few, questions were also set from Neo-Confucian texts, Diagram of the Supreme Ultimate, Tongshu, Western Inscription, and Correcting Ignorance.
translations.idiomatic: School entrance examinations at first required one Four Books essay and one discourse on the Classic of Filial Piety; when Filial Piety topics ran short, questions were also drawn from Neo-Confucian texts such as the Diagram of the Supreme Ultimate, Tongshu, Western Inscription, and Correcting Ignorance.

sentences.zh: 嗣定正試四書文二，覆試四書文、小學論各一。

translations.literal: Later the main examination was fixed at two Four Books essays; the re-examination one Four Books essay and one Elementary Learning discourse.
translations.idiomatic: Later the main test was fixed at two Four Books essays and the re-examination at one Four Books essay and one Elementary Learning discourse.

sentences.zh: 雍正初，科試加經文。

translations.literal: Early Yongzheng: triennial examinations added a classics essay.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Yongzheng, triennial examinations added a classics essay.

sentences.zh: 冬月晷短，書一、經一。

translations.literal: In winter when days were short, one essay and one classic.
translations.idiomatic: In winter, when daylight was short, one essay and one classic.

sentences.zh: 尋定科試四書、經文外，增策論題，仍用孝經。

translations.literal: Soon triennial examinations beyond Four Books and classics added policy-discourse topics, still using the Classic of Filial Piety.
translations.idiomatic: Soon triennial tests beyond Four Books and classics added policy essays, still drawing on the Classic of Filial Piety.

sentences.zh: 乾隆初，覆試兼用小學論。

translations.literal: Early Qianlong: re-examinations also included Elementary Learning discourses.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Qianlong, re-examinations also included Elementary Learning discourses.

sentences.zh: 中葉以後，試書藝、經藝各一。

translations.literal: In the mid-reign, essay and classic, one each.
translations.idiomatic: In the mid-reign, one literary essay and one classic essay.

sentences.zh: 增五言六韻詩。

translations.literal: Five-character regulated verse in six lines was added.
translations.idiomatic: Five-character regulated verse in six lines was added.

sentences.zh: 聖祖先後頒聖諭廣訓及訓飭士子文於直省儒學。

translations.literal: The Founding Emperors successively issued Sacred Edicts for Wide Instruction and admonitions to scholars to provincial Confucian schools.
translations.idiomatic: The early emperors successively issued the Sacred Edicts for Wide Instruction and admonitions to scholars for provincial schools.

sentences.zh: 雍正間，學士張照奏令儒童縣、府覆試，背錄聖諭廣訓一條，著為令。

translations.literal: In the Yongzheng period Academician Zhang Zhao memorialized requiring schoolboys at county and prefectural re-examinations to recite one article from the Sacred Edicts—made a permanent rule.
translations.idiomatic: In the Yongzheng period Academician Zhang Zhao required schoolboys at county and prefectural re-examinations to recite one passage from the Sacred Edicts, which became permanent rule.

sentences.zh: 凡新進生員，如國子監坐監例，令在學肄業，以次期新生入學為滿。

translations.literal: All newly admitted licentiates, like directorate students in residence, were required to pursue study at school until the next intake filled the quota.
translations.idiomatic: All newly admitted licentiates, like directorate students in residence, were required to study at school until the next intake filled the quota.

sentences.zh: 教官考校之法，有月課、季考，四書文外，兼試策論。

translations.literal: Methods for instructors' examination: monthly lessons and seasonal examinations; beyond Four Books essays, policy discourses were also tested.
translations.idiomatic: Instructors examined students through monthly lessons and seasonal tests; beyond Four Books essays, policy discourses were also required.

sentences.zh: 翌日講大清律刑名、錢穀要者若干條。

translations.literal: The next day several important articles on penal names in the Great Qing Code and on grain and revenue were lectured.
translations.idiomatic: The following day several key articles on penal law and fiscal administration in the Great Qing Code were lectured.

sentences.zh: 月集諸生明倫堂，誦訓飭士子文及臥碑諸條，諸生環聽。

translations.literal: Each month students assembled at the Hall of Bright Ethics; admonitions to scholars and reclining-stele articles were recited while students stood in a circle listening.
translations.idiomatic: Monthly, students assembled at the Hall of Bright Ethics to hear admonitions to scholars and the reclining-stele regulations read aloud.

sentences.zh: 除丁憂、患病、遊學、有事故外，不應月課三次者戒飭，無故終年不應者黜革。

translations.literal: Except for mourning leave, illness, study travel, or other cause, those missing monthly lessons three times were admonished; those absent without cause for a full year were dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: Except for mourning, illness, study travel, or other approved cause, three missed monthly lessons brought admonition; a full year of unjustified absence brought dismissal.

sentences.zh: 試卷申送學政查覆。

translations.literal: Examination papers were forwarded to the education commissioner for review.
translations.idiomatic: Examination papers were forwarded to the education commissioner for review.

sentences.zh: 訖於嘉慶，月課漸不舉行。

translations.literal: By the Jiaqing period monthly lessons were gradually abandoned.
translations.idiomatic: By the Jiaqing period monthly lessons had largely ceased.

sentences.zh: 御史辛從益以為言，詔令整頓。

translations.literal: Censor Xin Congyi spoke on this; an edict ordered rectification.
translations.idiomatic: Censor Xin Congyi raised the issue, and an edict ordered rectification.

sentences.zh: 嗣是教官多闒茸不稱職，有師生之名，無訓誨之實矣。

translations.literal: Thereafter instructors were mostly incompetent and unfit for office; there were names of teacher and student but no reality of instruction.
translations.idiomatic: Thereafter most instructors were mediocre and unfit; the names of teacher and student remained, but instruction was hollow.

sentences.zh: 學政考覈教官，按其文行及訓士勤惰，隨時薦黜。

translations.literal: Education commissioners examined instructors by their literary conduct and diligence in training scholars, recommending or dismissing at any time.
translations.idiomatic: Education commissioners evaluated instructors on literary conduct and diligence in training students, recommending or dismissing them as warranted.

sentences.zh: 康熙中，令撫臣考試。

translations.literal: In the Kangxi period governors were ordered to examine them.
translations.idiomatic: In the Kangxi period governors-general and governors were ordered to examine them.

sentences.zh: 嗣教職部選後，赴撫院試。

translations.literal: Later, after educational posts were selected by the ministry, appointees took examination at the governor's yamen.
translations.idiomatic: Later, after the Ministry selected educational appointees, they were examined at the governor's yamen before taking office.

sentences.zh: 四等以上，給憑赴任；

translations.literal: Fourth rank and above received credentials and proceeded to office;
translations.idiomatic: Those of fourth rank and above received credentials and took office;

sentences.zh: 五等學習三年再試，六等褫職。

translations.literal: fifth rank studied three years and were re-examined; sixth rank were dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: fifth rank studied three years and were re-examined; sixth rank were removed from office.

sentences.zh: 雍正初，定四、五等俱解任學習。

translations.literal: Early Yongzheng: fourth and fifth ranks were both released to study.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Yongzheng, both fourth- and fifth-rank failures were released to study further.

sentences.zh: 六年考成俸滿，盡心訓導，士無過犯者，督、撫、學政保題，擢用知縣。

translations.literal: Upon six-year completion of salary term, those who diligently instructed with no student offenses were recommended by governor, governor-general, and education commissioner for promotion to magistrate.
translations.idiomatic: After six years, instructors who had diligently taught without student misconduct were recommended by governor, governor-general, and education commissioner for promotion to magistrate.

sentences.zh: 學臣按臨，謁先師，升明倫堂，官生以次揖見。

translations.literal: When the education commissioner made his tour, he paid respects to the Master, ascended the Hall of Bright Ethics; official students bowed in turn.
translations.idiomatic: On tour, the education commissioner worshipped Confucius, ascended the Hall of Bright Ethics, and received successive bows from official students.

sentences.zh: 生員掣籤講書，各講大清律三條，西鄉立；

translations.literal: Licentiates drew lots to lecture on books and each lectured on three articles of the Great Qing Code, standing on the west side;
translations.idiomatic: Licentiates drew lots to lecture on the classics and each explained three articles of the Great Qing Code, standing on the west.

sentences.zh: 講畢，東鄉立：俟行賞罰。

translations.literal: when finished, they stood on the east side to await rewards and punishments.
translations.idiomatic: When finished, they stood on the east to await rewards and punishments.

sentences.zh: 考試生員，舊例歲、科試俱四書文二、經文一。

translations.literal: Examination of licentiates: by old rule both annual and triennial tests had two Four Books essays and one classic.
translations.idiomatic: Licentiate examinations: under the old rule both annual and triennial tests required two Four Books essays and one classic.

sentences.zh: 自有給燭之禁，例不出經題。

translations.literal: Since the prohibition on providing candles, classics topics were by rule not set.
translations.idiomatic: After candles were forbidden in the examination hall, classics topics were by rule omitted.

sentences.zh: 雍正元年，科試增經文，冬月一書、一經。

translations.literal: In Yongzheng 1, triennial tests added a classic; in winter one essay and one classic.
translations.idiomatic: In 1723 triennial tests added a classic essay; in winter, one essay and one classic.

sentences.zh: 六年，更定歲試兩書、一經，冬月一書、一經。

translations.literal: In year 6 it was changed: annual test two essays and one classic; winter one essay and one classic.
translations.idiomatic: In 1728 the annual test was set at two essays and one classic; winter at one essay and one classic.

sentences.zh: 科試書一、經一、策一，冬月減經文。

translations.literal: Triennial test one essay, one classic, one policy; in winter the classic was reduced.
translations.idiomatic: The triennial test required one essay, one classic, and one policy; in winter the classic was dropped.

sentences.zh: 乾隆二十三年，改歲試書一、經一，科試書一、策一、詩一，冬月亦如之。

translations.literal: In Qianlong 23, annual test changed to one essay and one classic; triennial to one essay, one policy, and one poem; winter likewise.
translations.idiomatic: In 1758 the annual test was one essay and one classic; the triennial, one essay, one policy, and one poem—with the same winter format.

sentences.zh: 欠考，勒限補行。

translations.literal: Absence from examination: deadline set for make-up.
translations.idiomatic: Absentees were given a deadline to make up the examination.

sentences.zh: 三次，黜革。

translations.literal: Three times, dismissal.
translations.idiomatic: After three absences, dismissal.

sentences.zh: 後寬其例，五次以上乃黜。

translations.literal: Later the rule was relaxed: only after five or more absences was dismissal applied.
translations.idiomatic: Later the rule was relaxed: dismissal came only after five or more absences.

sentences.zh: 駐防考試，清初定制，各省駐防弁兵子弟能讀書者，詣京應試。

translations.literal: Garrison examinations: under early Qing rules, sons of garrison officers and soldiers in the provinces who could read went to the capital to be examined.
