translations.idiomatic: Garrison examinations: under early Qing rules, literate sons of provincial garrison officers and soldiers traveled to the capital to test.

sentences.zh: 乾隆時，參領金珩請許歲、科試將軍先試騎射，就近送府院取進。

translations.literal: In the Qianlong period Deputy Commander Jin Hang requested that in annual and triennial tests the general first test archery and send candidates to the prefectural or provincial yamen for admission nearby.
translations.idiomatic: In the Qianlong period Deputy Commander Jin Hang asked that annual and triennial candidates first be tested in archery by the garrison general and then sent to nearby prefectural or provincial schools.

sentences.zh: 嚴旨切責。

translations.literal: A stern edict sharply rebuked this.
translations.idiomatic: A stern imperial edict sharply rebuked the proposal.

sentences.zh: 嘉慶四年，湖南布政使通恩奏如金珩言，詔議行。

translations.literal: In Jiaqing 4 Hunan provincial treasurer Tong En memorialized as Jin Hang had proposed; an edict ordered implementation.
translations.idiomatic: In 1799 Hunan provincial treasurer Tong En memorialized along the same lines, and an edict approved it.

sentences.zh: 應試童生，五六名取進一名，佐領約束之。

translations.literal: For examination schoolboys, one was admitted for every five or six; company commanders supervised them.
translations.idiomatic: One candidate was admitted for every five or six tested; company commanders supervised them.

sentences.zh: 訓習清語、騎射，府學課文藝。

translations.literal: They trained in Manchu language and archery; the prefectural school taught literary arts.
translations.idiomatic: They trained in Manchu and archery at the garrison; the prefectural school taught literary arts.

sentences.zh: 明年諭曰：「我滿洲根本，騎射為先。

translations.literal: The next year an edict stated: "Our Manchu foundation puts archery first.
translations.idiomatic: The next year an edict declared: "The Manchu foundation of our dynasty puts archery first.

sentences.zh: 若八旗子弟專以讀書應試為能，輕視弓馬，怠荒武備，殊失國家設立駐防之意。

translations.literal: If Banner sons take reading and examinations alone as their ability, slight bow and horse, neglect military preparedness—that gravely betrays the purpose of establishing garrisons.
translations.idiomatic: If Banner sons treat reading and examinations as their sole skill, slight archery, and neglect military training, they betray the very purpose of the garrisons.

sentences.zh: 嗣後各省駐防官弁子弟，不得因有就近考試之例，遂荒本業。」

translations.literal: Hereafter garrison officers' and soldiers' sons in the provinces must not, because of the nearby examination precedent, abandon their proper occupation."
translations.idiomatic: Hereafter sons of garrison officers and soldiers in the provinces must not, because examinations were made convenient, abandon their proper occupation."

translations.literal: The edict closed.
translations.idiomatic: The edict closed.

sentences.zh: 漢軍設廩、增，自順治九年始。

translations.literal: Han Banner grain-stipend and additional places began in Shunzhi 9.
translations.idiomatic: Grain-stipend and additional places for Han Banner licentiates began in 1652.

sentences.zh: 康熙十年，滿、蒙亦設廩、增。

translations.literal: In Kangxi 10 Manchu and Mongol also received grain-stipend and additional places.
translations.idiomatic: In 1671 Manchu and Mongol licentiates also received grain-stipend and additional places.

sentences.zh: 初制各二十名，嗣減漢軍十名。

translations.literal: At first each category had twenty places; later Han Banner was reduced by ten.
translations.idiomatic: At first each had twenty places; later Han Banner was reduced by ten.

sentences.zh: 雍正間定額，滿、蒙六十，漢軍三十。

translations.literal: In the Yongzheng period quotas were fixed: Manchu and Mongol 60, Han Banner 30.
translations.idiomatic: In the Yongzheng period quotas were fixed at 60 for Manchu and Mongol and 30 for Han Banner.

sentences.zh: 直省廩、增額，府四十，州三十，縣二十，衛十。

translations.literal: Provincial grain-stipend and additional quotas: prefectures 40, departments 30, counties 20, guards 10.
translations.idiomatic: Provincial grain-stipend and additional quotas were: prefectures 40, departments 30, counties 20, guards 10.

sentences.zh: 其新設者，府學視州學，州學視縣學。

translations.literal: For newly established schools, prefectural schools followed departmental quotas, departmental schools county quotas.
translations.idiomatic: For newly established schools, prefectural quotas followed departmental, and departmental followed county.

sentences.zh: 其一學分兩學，則均分其額，或差分之。

translations.literal: Where one school was divided into two, quotas were split equally or apportioned.
translations.idiomatic: Where one school was divided into two, quotas were split equally or apportioned between them.

sentences.zh: 六等黜陟法，視明為繁密。

translations.literal: The six-rank promotion and demotion law was more detailed than under the Ming.
translations.idiomatic: The six-rank promotion and demotion system was more detailed than under the Ming.

sentences.zh: 考列一等，增、附、青、社俱補廩。

translations.literal: First rank: additional, supplementary, green-gown, and community students all advanced to grain-stipend.
translations.idiomatic: First rank: additional, supplementary, green-gown, and community students all advanced to grain-stipend status.

sentences.zh: 無廩缺，附、青、社補增。

translations.literal: If no grain-stipend vacancy, supplementary, green-gown, and community students advanced to additional.
translations.idiomatic: Without a grain-stipend vacancy, supplementary, green-gown, and community students advanced to additional status.

sentences.zh: 無增缺，青、社復附，各候廩。

translations.literal: If no additional vacancy, green-gown and community students reverted to supplementary, each awaiting grain-stipend.
translations.idiomatic: Without an additional vacancy, green-gown and community students reverted to supplementary status and awaited grain-stipend.

sentences.zh: 原廩、增停降者收復。

translations.literal: Those whose original grain-stipend or additional status had been suspended or reduced were restored.
translations.idiomatic: Those whose grain-stipend or additional standing had been suspended or reduced were restored.

sentences.zh: 二等，增補廩，附、青、社補增。

translations.literal: Second rank: additional students advanced to grain-stipend; supplementary, green-gown, and community to additional.
translations.idiomatic: Second rank: additional students advanced to grain-stipend; supplementary, green-gown, and community students to additional.

sentences.zh: 無增缺，青、社復附。

translations.literal: If no additional vacancy, green-gown and community reverted to supplementary.
translations.idiomatic: Without an additional vacancy, green-gown and community students reverted to supplementary.

sentences.zh: 停廩降增者復廩。

translations.literal: Those suspended from grain-stipend and reduced to additional were restored to grain-stipend.
translations.idiomatic: Those suspended from grain-stipend and reduced to additional were restored to grain-stipend.

sentences.zh: 增降附者復增，不許補廩。

translations.literal: Those reduced from additional to supplementary were restored to additional; advancement to grain-stipend was not permitted.
translations.idiomatic: Those reduced from additional to supplementary were restored to additional but could not advance to grain-stipend.

sentences.zh: 三等，停廩者收復候廩。

translations.literal: Third rank: those suspended from grain-stipend were restored and awaited grain-stipend.
translations.idiomatic: Third rank: those suspended from grain-stipend were restored and placed on the waiting list for grain-stipend.

sentences.zh: 丁憂起復，病痊考復，緣事辨復，增降附者許收復，青衣發社者復附，廩降增者不許復。

translations.literal: Resumption after mourning, restoration after illness and examination, restoration after deliberation on cause—additional reduced to supplementary might be restored; green-gown sent to community schools reverted to supplementary; grain-stipend reduced to additional might not be restored.
translations.idiomatic: Restoration after mourning, after recovery from illness and re-examination, or after review of special cases was permitted; green-gown students sent to community schools reverted to supplementary status; those reduced from grain-stipend to additional could not be restored.

sentences.zh: 四等，廩免責停餼，不作缺，限讀書六月送考。

translations.literal: Fourth rank: grain-stipend students were exempted from blame but grain suspended, no vacancy created; limited to six months of study before sending to examination.
translations.idiomatic: Fourth rank: grain-stipend students were spared punishment but lost stipends without vacating their places; they had six months to study before re-examination.

sentences.zh: 停降者不許限考。

translations.literal: Those under suspension and reduction were not permitted the limited examination.
translations.idiomatic: Those under suspension or reduction were not permitted the limited re-examination.

sentences.zh: 增、附、青、社俱撲責。

translations.literal: Additional, supplementary, green-gown, and community students all received paddling and reproof.
translations.idiomatic: Additional, supplementary, green-gown, and community students all received corporal punishment and reproof.

sentences.zh: 五等，廩停作缺。

translations.literal: Fifth rank: grain-stipend suspension created a vacancy.
translations.idiomatic: Fifth rank: grain-stipend suspension created a vacancy.

sentences.zh: 原停廩者降增，增降附，附降青衣，青衣發社，原發社者黜為民。

translations.literal: Those originally suspended from grain-stipend were reduced to additional; additional to supplementary; supplementary to green-gown; green-gown sent to community schools; those originally sent to community schools were dismissed as commoners.
translations.idiomatic: Those suspended from grain-stipend were reduced to additional; additional to supplementary; supplementary to green-gown; green-gown to community school; those already in community schools were dismissed as commoners.

sentences.zh: 六等，廩膳十年以上發社，六年以上與增十年以上者，發本處充吏，餘黜為民。

translations.literal: Sixth rank: grain-stipend students of ten years or more were sent to community schools; those of six years or more together with additional students of ten years or more were sent to serve as clerks locally; the rest dismissed as commoners.
translations.idiomatic: Sixth rank: grain-stipend students of ten years or more were sent to community schools; those of six years or more, together with additional students of ten years or more, were made local clerks; the rest were dismissed as commoners.

sentences.zh: 入學未及六年者發社。

translations.literal: Those who had entered school less than six years were sent to community schools.
translations.idiomatic: Students enrolled less than six years were sent to community schools.

sentences.zh: 科試一、二等送鄉試，幫補廩、增，如歲試大率祗列三等，八旗生員給錢糧，考列四等以下停給，次屆列一、二、三等給還。

translations.literal: First and second ranks in triennial examination were sent to provincial examination; grain-stipend and additional places were supplemented as in annual examination, which generally listed only third rank; Eight Banners licentiates received grain pay—those ranked fourth or below had pay stopped; if next session they ranked first, second, or third, pay was restored.
translations.idiomatic: Triennial first- and second-rank students went to the provincial examination; grain-stipend and additional places were filled as in the annual test, which usually listed only third rank. Eight Banners licentiates received grain pay; fourth rank or below lost it, restored if they ranked first through third the next session.

sentences.zh: 優等補廩、增，劣等降青、社，如漢生員。

translations.literal: Superior ranks supplemented grain-stipend and additional; inferior ranks reduced to green-gown and community—as with Han licentiates.
translations.idiomatic: Superior ranks advanced to grain-stipend or additional; inferior ranks were reduced to green-gown or community status, as with Han licentiates.

sentences.zh: 八旗故重騎射，往往不苛求文藝，但置後等。

translations.literal: The Eight Banners therefore valued archery; they often did not demand literary arts strictly but placed such students in lower ranks.
translations.idiomatic: The Eight Banners valued archery highly and often did not strictly demand literary accomplishment, placing weaker students in lower ranks.

sentences.zh: 凡優恤諸生，例免差徭。

translations.literal: All preferential treatment of students: by precedent they were exempt from corvée and levies.
translations.idiomatic: Licentiates enjoyed preferential treatment and were by precedent exempt from corvée and levies.

sentences.zh: 廩生貧生給學租養贍。

translations.literal: Impoverished grain-stipend students received school rent for support.
translations.idiomatic: Impoverished grain-stipend students received school rents for their support.

sentences.zh: 違犯禁令，小者府、州、縣行教官責懲，大者申學政，黜革後治罪，地方官不得擅責。

translations.literal: Violations of prohibitions: minor ones were punished by prefectural, departmental, or county instructors; major ones were reported to the education commissioner, dismissed and then punished—local officials might not punish on their own authority.
translations.idiomatic: Minor violations were punished by prefectural, departmental, or county instructors; major ones were reported to the education commissioner for dismissal and subsequent punishment—local officials could not punish licentiates on their own authority.

sentences.zh: 學政校文外，賞黜優劣，以為勸懲。

translations.literal: Beyond examining papers, the education commissioner rewarded the excellent and punished the inferior as encouragement and warning.
translations.idiomatic: Beyond grading examinations, the education commissioner rewarded excellence and punished failure as encouragement and deterrent.

sentences.zh: 如教官徇庇劣生不揭報，或經揭報，學政不嚴加懲處，分別罰俸、鐫級、褫職。

translations.literal: If instructors shielded inferior students and did not report them, or if reported the education commissioner did not punish severely—salary fines, grade reduction, or dismissal applied by distinction.
translations.idiomatic: If instructors shielded poor students or the education commissioner failed to punish reported cases, penalties ranged from salary fines and demotion to dismissal.

sentences.zh: 其大較也。

translations.literal: Such were the general outlines.
translations.idiomatic: Such were the general outlines of the system.

sentences.zh: 光緒末，科舉廢，丙午並停歲、科試。

translations.literal: In late Guangxu the examination system was abolished; in bingwu both annual and triennial tests were stopped.
translations.idiomatic: In late Guangxu the examination system was abolished; in 1906 both annual and triennial school examinations ceased.

sentences.zh: 天下生員無所託業，乃議廣用途，許考各部院謄錄。

translations.literal: Licentiates throughout the realm had nowhere to pursue their occupation; it was proposed to broaden their use and permit examination for transcription posts in ministries and courts.
translations.idiomatic: With examinations ended, licentiates nationwide lacked occupation; the court proposed broader employment and examinations for transcription posts in ministries and courts.

sentences.zh: 並於考優年，令州縣官、教官會保申送督、撫、學政，考取文理暢達、事理明晰者，大省百名，中省七十名，小省五十名，咨部以巡檢、典史分別註選，或分發試用。

translations.literal: Also in years of superior examination, prefectural and county officials and instructors were to jointly recommend and forward through governor, governor-general, and education commissioner those of fluent style and clear reasoning—large provinces 100, medium 70, small 50—to the ministry for registration as patrol inspectors or clerks by distinction, or for probationary appointment.
translations.idiomatic: In years of superior examination, officials and instructors were to recommend candidates of fluent style and clear reasoning—100 for large provinces, 70 medium, 50 small—for registration as patrol inspectors or clerks, or probationary appointment.

sentences.zh: 各省學政改司，考校學堂。

translations.literal: Provincial education commissioners were changed to bureaus examining modern schools.
translations.idiomatic: Provincial education commissioners were reorganized into bureaus supervising modern schools.

sentences.zh: 未幾學政裁，教官停選。

translations.literal: Soon education commissioners were abolished and instructor selection stopped.
translations.idiomatic: Soon education commissioners were abolished and selection of instructors ceased.

sentences.zh: 在職者，凡生員考職、孝廉方正各事屬之，俸滿用知縣，或以直州同、鹽庫大使用。

translations.literal: Those still in office handled licentiate examinations for office, filial integrity and probity nominations, and related matters; upon salary term completion they were used as magistrates, or as subprefects of directly administered departments or salt treasury superintendents.
translations.idiomatic: Those remaining in office handled licentiate qualification examinations, filial integrity nominations, and related matters; at term they might become magistrates, subprefects, or salt treasury superintendents.

sentences.zh: 儒學雖不廢，名存實亡，非一日矣。

translations.literal: Though Confucian schools were not abolished, name survived while substance perished—not for a single day only.
translations.idiomatic: Confucian schools were not formally abolished, but they had long been hollow in substance.

sentences.zh: 武生附儒學，通稱武生。

translations.literal: Military students were attached to Confucian schools and were commonly called military students.
translations.idiomatic: Military students were attached to Confucian schools and were commonly called military licentiates.

sentences.zh: 順治初，京衛武生童考試隸兵部。

translations.literal: Early Shunzhi: capital guard military students' child examinations were under the Ministry of War.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Shunzhi, child examinations for capital guard military students were under the Ministry of War.

sentences.zh: 康熙三年，改隸學院，直省府、州、縣、衛武生，儒學教官兼轄之。

translations.literal: In Kangxi 3 this was changed to the education bureau; military students of provincial prefectures, departments, counties, and guards were jointly supervised by Confucian school instructors.
translations.idiomatic: In 1664 they were placed under the education bureau; provincial military students were jointly supervised by Confucian school instructors.

sentences.zh: 騎射外，教以武經七書、百將傳及孝經、四書。

translations.literal: Beyond archery, they were taught the Seven Military Classics, Hundred Generals' Biographies, and the Classic of Filial Piety and Four Books.
translations.idiomatic: Beyond archery, they studied the Seven Military Classics, Hundred Generals' Biographies, the Classic of Filial Piety, and the Four Books.

sentences.zh: 學政三年一考。

translations.literal: The education commissioner examined them once every three years.
translations.idiomatic: The education commissioner examined them every three years.

sentences.zh: 順天舊設武學，自八旗設儒學教官，兼轄滿洲、蒙古、漢軍武生，裁武學官。

translations.literal: Shuntian formerly had a military school; after the Eight Banners established Confucian instructors who jointly supervised Manchu, Mongol, and Han Banner military students, the military school office was cut.
translations.idiomatic: Shuntian once had a military school; after Eight Banners Confucian instructors took charge of Manchu, Mongol, and Han Banner military students, the military school office was abolished.

sentences.zh: 大、宛兩縣武生，順天教官轄之，學額如文生童例，分大、中、小學。

translations.literal: Military students of Daxing and Wanping counties were under Shuntian instructors; quotas followed civil schoolboy precedent, divided large, medium, and small.
translations.idiomatic: Military students of Daxing and Wanping were under Shuntian instructors, with quotas like civil schoolboys divided among large, medium, and small schools.

sentences.zh: 自二十名遞減至七八名。

translations.literal: From twenty places this was progressively reduced to seven or eight.
translations.idiomatic: Quotas were progressively reduced from twenty to seven or eight.

sentences.zh: 考試分內、外場，先外場騎射，次內場策論。

translations.literal: Examinations were divided into inner and outer fields: first outer-field archery, then inner-field policy discourse.
translations.idiomatic: Examinations had outer and inner sessions: archery first, then policy essays indoors.

sentences.zh: 歲試列一、二等，准作科舉。

translations.literal: First and second rank in annual examination qualified for military licentiate status.
translations.idiomatic: First- and second-rank annual examination results qualified students as military licentiates.

sentences.zh: 故武生有歲試無科試。

translations.literal: Therefore military students had annual but not triennial examinations.
translations.idiomatic: Military students thus had annual but not triennial examinations.

sentences.zh: 各省書院之設，輔學校所不及，初於省會設之。

translations.literal: Establishment of provincial academies supplemented what schools could not reach; at first they were set up in provincial capitals.
translations.idiomatic: Provincial academies supplemented what official schools could not provide; they were first established in provincial capitals.

sentences.zh: 世祖頒給帑金，風勵天下。

translations.literal: The Founding Emperor distributed treasury funds to encourage the realm.
translations.idiomatic: The Shunzhi Emperor distributed treasury funds to encourage academies throughout the realm.

sentences.zh: 厥後府、州、縣次第建立，延聘經明行修之士為之長，秀異多出其中。

translations.literal: Thereafter prefectures, departments, and counties established them in succession, engaging scholars accomplished in classics and conduct as directors; many outstanding talents came from them.
translations.idiomatic: Prefectures, departments, and counties then followed, engaging scholars of classical learning and moral conduct as directors; many outstanding men emerged from them.

sentences.zh: 高宗明詔獎勸，比於古者侯國之學。

translations.literal: Emperor Gaozong issued clear edicts of reward, comparing them to the schools of feudal states in antiquity.
translations.idiomatic: The Qianlong Emperor issued clear edicts of encouragement, comparing academies to the schools of ancient feudal states.

sentences.zh: 儒學浸衰，教官不舉其職，所賴以造士者，獨在書院。

translations.literal: As Confucian schools declined and instructors failed their duties, cultivation of talent depended alone on academies.
translations.idiomatic: As Confucian schools declined and instructors neglected their duties, talent cultivation depended almost solely on academies.

sentences.zh: 其裨益育才，非淺鮮也。

translations.literal: Their benefit in nurturing talent was no small matter.
translations.idiomatic: Their contribution to nurturing talent was considerable.

sentences.zh: 又有義學，社學。

translations.literal: There were also charity schools and community schools.
translations.idiomatic: There were also charity schools and community schools.

sentences.zh: 社學，鄉置一區，擇文行優者充社師，免其差徭，量給廩餼。

translations.literal: Community schools: one per rural district; men of superior literary conduct and behavior served as community teachers, exempt from corvée, with grain stipends as appropriate.
translations.idiomatic: Community schools were set up one per rural district; men of superior conduct served as teachers, exempt from corvée and given grain stipends as appropriate.

sentences.zh: 凡近鄉子弟十二歲以上令入學。

translations.literal: All local boys twelve years and above were ordered to enter school.
translations.idiomatic: All local boys aged twelve or above were required to attend.

sentences.zh: 義學，初由京師五城各立一所，後各省府、州、縣多設立，教孤寒生童，或苗、蠻、黎、瑤子弟秀異者。

translations.literal: Charity schools: at first one was established in each of the five wards of the capital; later many were set up in provincial prefectures, departments, and counties, teaching impoverished schoolboys or gifted sons of Miao, Man, Li, and Yao peoples.
translations.idiomatic: Charity schools began with one in each of the capital's five wards; later many provinces established them to teach impoverished boys or gifted sons of Miao, Man, Li, and Yao peoples.

sentences.zh: 規制簡略，可無述也。

translations.literal: Regulations were simple; they need not be described.
translations.idiomatic: Their regulations were simple and need not be described here.
